Get started

A starter kit, not a finished system

A Figma library and a token layer built so that a new client project can be retoned in a day, and so that an engineer or a coding agent can read the result without anyone translating it first.

DesignerEngineerBoth readingThe first hour path for designers.The first hour path for engineers.Both first hour paths side by side.

8collections

313component variants
87module sets
9page templates
146icons, 4 libraries
24interaction specs

The one thing to understand first

Tier 1 is the entire adaptation surface. Nothing above 01 Primitives holds a raw value. Semantic tokens alias primitives, component tokens alias semantics, and no layer in any component holds a hex of its own. Retone the 147 primitive rows and the change reaches all 69 component sets and 87 module sets without anybody opening a component.

That is also why the primitives are scope hidden in Figma. A designer picking a colour sees the semantic roles, not the ramp, so nobody reaches past the layer that is supposed to be doing the work.

How to adapt this kit

This is a starting point, and everything below Tier 1 is already wired. When a new project lands you change raw values in one place and let the rest follow. Work through the checklist in order.

The one rule. Tier 1 primitives are the entire adaptation surface. If re-skinning a project makes you open Tier 2 or Tier 3, the kit has a bug. Tell whoever maintains it instead of editing around it, because once project files start carrying local fixes the kit stops being worth duplicating.
Edit this01 Primitives

Raw values: brand ramps, the two type families, spacing and radius. The whole adaptation surface.

Inherits02 Semantic

Design intent: text/default, action/primary, surface/raised. Identical names on every project.

Inherits03 Component

One token per component slot. The only layer dev code references.

Per breakpoint04 Responsive

Grid and display type across Desktop, Tablet and Mobile modes.

How this maps to the Playbook

The Design System Playbook sets the sequence. The kit has the first three steps already done, so a new project starts at step four. The Playbook is still what goes to the client; this file is the internal head start.

  1. 1
    Build primitives first Done in kit

    147 primitives across colour, type, space, radius, stroke, opacity and motion.

  2. 2
    Create doc templates Done in kit

    Read Me, Foundations, Token Reference, Iconography, Image System, Interactions, Governance.

  3. 3
    Import components Done in kit

    69 sets and 313 variants, every property bound to Tier 3. Above them, 87 module sets and nine page templates.

  4. 4
    Review iteratively, not upfront Your job

    On a project the iteration budget moves from discovery to adaptation. Step 6 of the checklist below is that checkpoint.

  5. 5
    Package the written reference doc Part done

    The Token Reference page ships with the kit. The client-facing write-up is still per project.

Adaptation checklist

In order. Later steps assume the earlier ones propagated. Steps 02, 03, 06 and 07 have depth behind them: see the adaptation runbook on the Governance page for the rungs a client palette has to supply and what has to be re-measured once it moves.

  1. 01

    Duplicate this file. Rename to <Client>_DS_v1. Update the Cover.

  2. 02

    Set type/family/display and type/family/text in 01 Primitives. Load the client fonts in Figma first or the change fails silently. Pick the icon library in 06 Icon Library (Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor or Remix) and make it the file default. Paste the client logo into the two Logo Slot variants on Components (Full and Mark); every header and footer follows.

  3. 03

    Replace the brand and accent ramps in 01 Primitives. Revalue the steps, never delete one. A deleted step breaks every alias above it.

  4. 04

    Set grid columns, margin and gutter per breakpoint in 04 Responsive.

  5. 05

    Set the display type scale per breakpoint in 04 Responsive.

  6. 06

    STOP. Walk Foundations and Components without editing anything. Everything should have re-skinned. If it did not, find the broken alias. Do not hand-fix the component.

  7. 07

    Contrast pass. AA minimum on text, AAA on primary action and error, 3.0 on the focus ring and on icons as they render in the chosen library (Phosphor is the light one). Compute the ratios, do not eyeball them.

  8. 08

    Image System: confirm the ratio set, empty the module mapping, pick or write the platform sheet.

  9. 09

    Only now add or remove components and modules, and only where the client needs one. Delete the optional Landing, Ecommerce or Dashboard page if the project has no use for it; nothing outside the page references it. Dropping Ecommerce also drops four entries on the Interactions page: Carousel, Add to bag, Cart drawer and mini cart, and Countdown. Wire anything new to Tier 3.

  10. 10

    Fill the Interactions page for any non-standard behaviour.

  11. 11

    Seed the Governance tracker with the project touchpoints and waves.

  12. 12

    Export tokens once the dev platform is confirmed: Token Studio, Zeroheight, or custom.

  13. 13

    Publish as a library. Log anything the kit could not absorb and feed it back.

Naming

Two conventions, one source. The slash gives Figma its grouping and the hyphen is what CSS accepts. The export derives the second from the first, so neither is hand-maintained and neither should be "fixed" to match the other.

LayerConventionExample
Figma variable pathslash-delimited, lowercase, numeric stepscomponent/button/primary/background
CSS custom propertysame path, hyphen-flattened--component-button-primary-background

Use

  • color/brand/500
  • text/muted
  • action/primary

Avoid

  • color/nightsky/500 poetic family name
  • color/brand-500 breaks Figma grouping
  • text/gray describes appearance

What the kit leaves out

  • Client modules. The module pages are a generic floor: sixteen global modules plus optional landing, retail and dashboard pages. What made a past client's modules valuable was that they were that client’s site, and that part stays project work.
  • No code pipeline. Style Dictionary, an npm package and CI sync need an engineer and a real repo; propose that separately.
  • No live data or behaviour. Charts carry sample data, and hover, focus and tooltips are drawn as static variants. Anything a frame cannot show belongs on the Interactions page and in the build.
  • No client-facing narrative. The Design System Playbook owns the case for design systems and the process story. Link to it, don’t restate it here.

Read Me in Figma

Your first hour designer

  1. Turn the library on. Components, Iconography and Image System publish as one library. Enable it in the project file before you draw anything.
  2. Retone 01 Primitives. 120 of the 147 rows are load-bearing: neutral, brand, accent, utility, chart, and the alpha steps the shadows use. Client adaptation lists exactly which rungs a client palette has to supply, and the prompt that runs the whole job.
  3. Set the modes on the top level frame. Semantic carries Light and Dark, Spacing carries Comfortable and Compact, Responsive carries Desktop, Tablet and Mobile. Children inherit.
  4. Build from sets, never from copies. If a component needs a decision the kit does not have, add a row to 03 Component. Do not paint a layer.
  5. Read the description first. Every set says what it is for and where it stops. The ones with real prose are the ones that get argued about.

Your first hour engineer

  1. Take the token layer whole. Eight collections, 543 shipping rows. 05 Docs styles the documentation and stays behind.
  2. Keep the names. A token name maps to a custom property by swapping slashes for dashes. Tier 3 alone takes a component prefix, so button/primary/background becomes --component-button-primary-background.
  3. Wire the two motion modes. Full is the default. Reduced collapses every transition duration to 0 and leaves the waits and the curves untouched.
  4. Build behaviour from the interaction specs. Twenty four of them, each naming the tokens it uses and the CSS it expects. They are the contract, not a suggestion.
  5. Never hardcode a duration. Figma cannot bind one, so the Figma file names durations in prose and the token layer is the only place they are real.

Two readings of the same system

The Reading control in the header changes what every page on this site shows, not just how it is worded. Designer gives you Figma token names, the properties panel, and what to set on a frame. Engineer gives you CSS custom properties, the interaction prompt blocks, and what to define in code. Both shows the two side by side, which is the one to use when a designer and an engineer are looking at the same screen and need to agree that button/primary/background and --component-button-primary-background are the same decision.

The choice is remembered, so you land back in the reading you left in.

Where this site ends and the file begins. Specs, indexes and the interaction prompts live here because they get copied. The long form notes on each component live in the Figma description, because that is where somebody reads them while they are using the thing. Every section on this site links back to its sheet: open the file.

The eleven sheets

Eleven sheets, each its own frame so a single foundation can be selected, exported or linked by node id rather than cropped out of one tall canvas. Tier 1 primitives come first, then the tier 2 layers that give them meaning: the semantic colour map, and the spacing scale that carries the density modes. Every value is a placeholder: revalue the steps when adapting and never delete one.

  1. 01Colour · Primitive rampsBrand, accent, neutral
  2. 02Colour · UtilitySuccess, warning, error, info

Colour

The kit ships neutral on purpose. Brand and accent are real ramps so the structure can be tested, but they are placeholders, and the whole point of tier 1 is that they get replaced. Nothing in the kit argues for a hue.

There is one documented exception. surface/selected is a brand tint, because a selected row has to read as chosen and no neutral does that job while sitting next to a hover ground. Every tinted badge on a selected row therefore carries a mid rung edge, since a pale fill reads by hue rather than by lightness and badge/info/background against brand/100 measures a contrast ratio of 1.005.

Primitive ramps

Brand and accent carry ten steps, neutral thirteen. Every other colour group the client has, such as web, category or pop colours, gets an eleven step ramp row per colour here, under the group’s own name, with the client hex kept at its nearest rung. Revalue the steps when adapting; never delete one, because a deleted step breaks every alias above it. The values here are washed out so nobody mistakes them for a real brand.

Utility families

Three steps per family and no more. These four cover feedback states only. For anything else, reach for brand or neutral.

Intent, not appearance

These names are identical on every project. Only what they point at changes, and they change automatically when Tier 1 does. Switch this collection between Light and Dark to check both.

Data visualisation

The palette was computed, not chosen. Eight hues in a fixed order, validated in both modes against colour vision deficiency simulation and against normal vision, with the slot order itself doing the safety work. Assign slots in sequence and never cycle them.

The three series cap. Scatter, bubble, choropleth and small multiples carry a three series cap. Past three, fold to Other or facet. Adjacent checking is enough for a stack, a bar or a line, because only neighbours ever touch. A scatter, a bubble chart, a choropleth or a set of small multiples puts any two marks side by side, and at that harder test no ordering of eight hues clears the floors. Cutting series is the fix, not restepping the palette.

One hue, light to dark, for continuous magnitude. The anchor flips in dark mode so the lightest step still means near zero.

Diverging

Blue against red, with a neutral grey midpoint and an equal number of steps per arm. Never a hue at the middle.

Ordinal is a different test. A discrete ordered ramp has to stay readable at the end nearest the surface. Light mode starts no lighter than 300. Dark mode goes no darker than 500. The red arm skips 400: the step from 300 sits at delta L 0.051, under the 0.06 floor.

Every slot clears a 3.0 contrast ratio on both chart surfaces, measured against #FFFFFF in light and #242628 in dark, so no relief channel is needed to make a mark visible. Identity is a separate obligation. Two or more series always carry a legend, four or fewer are also directly labelled, and a status colour never stands in for a series.

Data visualisation sheet in Figma

A chart palette is computable, so it was computed rather than picked. Eight categorical hues in a fixed order, one sequential ramp, one diverging pair, and a set of chart chrome tokens. The order is the colour-blind safety mechanism and does not change. The kit’s four status colours are reserved and never used as a series. The eleven chart families and five chart parts on Components bind these roles and nothing else, so a retone reaches every series.

What was measured

Light   worst adjacent CVD dE 9.1   normal-vision dE 17.1   all 8 slots >= 3:1 on surface/page
Dark    worst adjacent CVD dE 9.1   normal-vision dE 15.6   all 8 slots >= 3:1 on surface/page
All-pairs forms (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small multiples) carry a 3 series cap:
  slots 1 to 3 clear all pairs in both modes, CVD dE 9.3 and normal-vision 20.8 light, 17.4 dark.
  Past three, fold the rest into Other or facet. Adding a ninth hue is never the answer.
Targets: CVD dE >= 8 under protanopia and deuteranopia, normal-vision dE >= 15, marks >= 3:1.

Rules

  • Assign slots in order and never cycle. A ninth series folds into Other, or the chart becomes small multiples.
  • One axis. Two measures at different scales are two charts, never two y scales on one.
  • Colour follows the entity, not its rank. A filter that drops a series must not repaint the survivors.
  • Status colour is reserved. A series that means good or bad wears the status tokens; a series that is just series 4 wears a categorical slot. Never both in one chart.
  • Chart text wears text tokens, never the series colour. A coloured mark next to the label carries the identity.
  • Two or more series always get a legend, and up to four are also labelled directly, so identity is never colour alone.

Sequential

One hue, magnitude only. Step 1 sits nearest the surface, so the anchor flips between modes rather than the meaning inverting. For discrete ordered marks start at step 3 in Light and stop at step 5 in Dark, so the end nearest the surface still clears 2:1.

Diverging

Red for the negative arm, blue for the positive, neutral grey at the midpoint so zero reads as nothing. Never a hue in the middle, and never a rainbow.

Elevation

Four effect styles, and every one of them binds its colour to a semantic token rather than carrying a hex. In dark mode the alpha steps get heavier, because a shadow on a dark ground has less to work with.

Elevation sheet in Figma

Elevation is four effect styles, not a scale anyone can invent a fifth step of. Each one is a single drop shadow whose colour is bound to a token, so the shadow gets heavier in Dark rather than disappearing into the ground.

LevelShadowUsed for
Flatno shadowApplied on purpose, so a flat surface is a decision rather than an omission. Card Flat uses it.
Raisedy 2 · blur 8 · elevation/shadow-raisedA card or a row lifted a little off the page.
Overlayy 8 · blur 24 · elevation/shadow-overlayFloats over the page and is dismissed by the next click: menu, select list, tooltip, toast.
Modaly 16 · blur 48 · elevation/shadow-modalThe one surface that takes the screen: modal and drawer.

Styles and their scale tokens

Inter is a placeholder for both display and text. The eleven page styles are bound to a scale/* token, so the sizes change with the breakpoint mode rather than by hand. The seven UI styles are what text inside a component uses; they bind a fixed type/size step, because a button label or a table cell does not grow with the viewport. All eighteen bind family, weight and size to variables, so a client typeface reaches every one.

Spacing and density

Three families of step, and the family says what the gap is for rather than how big it is: inset is padding inside a thing, inline is the gap between things on a row, stack is the gap between stacked things. All three share the same nine steps and the same aliases, so a component that uses inset/lg and one that uses stack/lg stay in step with each other when the scale moves.

Compact is not a smaller copy of Comfortable. The small steps hold, because 2px and 4px are already doing the least they can, and the middle and upper steps pull in. Density is set per frame, so one screen in a project can be dense without the whole project becoming dense.

The spacing scale

Two layers. Tier 1 is a 4px grid of raw steps, scope-hidden so nothing binds to it directly. Tier 2 names those steps by intent and carries the density modes, and it is the layer a component actually binds to. Every padding and gap in the library resolves through it.

Tier 1, the 4px grid: space/0 0px · space/2 2px · space/4 4px · space/8 8px · space/12 12px · space/16 16px · space/20 20px · space/24 24px · space/32 32px · space/40 40px · space/48 48px · space/56 56px · space/64 64px · space/80 80px · space/96 96px

The number is the same across the three families. The prefix is what tells you, and a client, what the number is for, so tightening the rows in a table does not also tighten every padding in the product.

inset/*

Padding inside a container. Card padding, button padding, the space between a panel edge and its content.

stack/*

Vertical gap between stacked items. Label above input, rows in a menu, blocks in a card.

inline/*

Horizontal gap between items in a row. Icon to label, buttons in an action bar, cells in a row.

What each step is for

StepTypical use
2xsText pairs that read as one block, like a name over a role.
xsIcon to label in a small pill. The tightest gap the system allows.
smIcon to label at normal size, and the default for tight rows.
mdThe workhorse. Field and button padding, most row gaps.
lgAccordion padding, comfortable row gaps.
xlTable and list row padding.
2xlCard and button inline padding. The default container inset.
3xlModal padding, generous panels.
4xlLarge panels and anything that needs to feel deliberately open.

Switching density

The 02 Spacing collection has two modes. Because every padding and gap in the library binds to it, pinning a frame to Compact tightens the whole thing at once. The two boards below are the same four components; the only difference is the mode each board is pinned to.

Select any frame and set the 02 Spacing mode in the right panel, the same way you switch Light and Dark. Everything inside inherits it, so one setting on a page frame changes the density of every component on that page.

Density is a separate axis from breakpoint. 04 Responsive still controls grid, margins and section rhythm per Desktop, Tablet and Mobile, and the two compose: a Compact mobile frame is a legitimate combination. Figma allows one mode axis per collection, which is exactly why these are two collections rather than one.

Pick one as the project default and stay with it. Compact exists for dense internal tools, not as a per-screen decision. Two densities inside one product reads as two products.

Rules and coverage

Spacing only behaves like a system if everything actually resolves through it. These numbers are counted from this file, so they cannot drift.

Across 69 component setsCount
Paddings bound to a token698
Gaps bound to a token429
Still a literal number199 (off the 4px grid, listed below)
inset · stack · inline in use445 · 175 · 254
Tier 3 spacing tokens12, all now resolving through tier 2

Four rules

  • No margins. Figma has padding and gap, and that is the whole vocabulary. A margin typed into a nudge is invisible to the token layer and to the developer reading the handoff, and it is the single most common reason a spacing system stops working.
  • No raw numbers. If a padding or gap is not bound to an inset, stack or inline token, it will not move when the brand or the density does. 199 values are still literal, and none of them sits on the 4px grid, so none has a token to bind to: Swatch 96, Combobox 31, Date Picker 17, Tracker 16, Icon Button 12, Steps 9, Menu 8, File Row 6, Skeleton Module and Order Line 1 each, and the 2 Link underline offsets, which are an optical detail rather than layout. Each needs a design decision, 16 or 20 rather than 18, before it can bind.
  • Everything sits on the 4px grid. If a design needs 18px, the honest answers are 16 or 20. Reaching for 18 means either the scale is wrong or the composition is, and it is almost always the composition.
  • Pick the family by what the gap does, not by its size. A 12px icon-to-label gap is inline/md and a 12px stack of rows is stack/md. They resolve to the same number today, which is precisely why the names matter: a client can tighten rows without touching padding.

How a spacing value resolves

01 Primitives  space/24
  02 Spacing  inset/2xl   Comfortable 24 · Compact 20
    03 Component  card/padding
      Card, padding on all four sides

A component slot that is part of the component API gets a tier 3 token, the way card/padding and button/primary/padding-inline do. Internal composition gaps bind straight to tier 2, because the gap between an icon and its label is not something a developer references by name.

Tier 4 keeps the spacing that changes with the breakpoint rather than the density: grid/gutter, grid/margin, space/section-gap, space/section-padding-block and its compact partner space/section-padding-block-sm, plus space/content-gap and space/content-gap-lg for the gaps between blocks inside a band. Those are a different axis and compose with the density modes.

Grid

Three column counts, drawn below to scale, and one grid style in Figma that covers all three. The columns are a layout aid, not a promise. A table, a product grid or a card row lands on them; a hero image or a full bleed band is allowed to ignore them, and the margin is the only part that never moves.

Columns are the thing that actually changes across breakpoints. Twelve divides by two, three, four and six, which is why a desktop grid can carry a three up product row and a two up feature block without a special case. Eight keeps halves and quarters on tablet. Four on mobile is really one column plus the ability to split a row in half.

Gutters stay put between tablet and mobile. Both sit at 16, so the thing that changes going to mobile is the column count and the margin, not the rhythm inside the content. That is deliberate: a gutter that shrinks with the screen makes a two up mobile row read as one block.

Applying it in Figma

There is one grid style in the file, called Grid/Responsive columns, and it is right at every breakpoint. Its column count, gutter and margin are bound to grid/columns, grid/gutter and grid/margin, so the grid reads the 04 Responsive mode on the frame rather than carrying numbers of its own.

So there is nothing to choose. Apply the style, set the frame to Desktop, Tablet or Mobile, and the grid becomes 12, 8 or 4 columns with the matching gutter and margin. Three separate styles would have been three things to keep in step, and the first one to drift would be the one nobody noticed.

Never type a column count into a frame. A hand set grid is the one that goes stale when the tokens move.

In code

All five numbers come from 04 Responsive, so a breakpoint is one place to change:

  • --grid-columns, --grid-gutter, --grid-margin
  • --layout-canvas-width, --layout-content-max

The container is --layout-content-max wide with --grid-margin either side, and the tracks are repeat(var(--grid-columns), minmax(0, 1fr)) with a gap of var(--grid-gutter). Because grid/columns is a real number token rather than a breakpoint name, the same rule holds at all three sizes and only the custom property values change.

Notes

  • Apply the grid with the Grid/Responsive columns style rather than typing a column count. It is the only grid style in the file, and it is right at every breakpoint because all three of its numbers are bound to tokens. A hand typed grid is the one that goes stale.
  • To work at a breakpoint, duplicate its frame above. The column grid and the pinned mode come with it, so type and spacing resolve without a single manual resize.
  • To pin a frame you built yourself, select it and set the 04 Responsive mode in the right panel. A frame with no explicit mode inherits from its parent, which is usually what you want inside a page but not at the top level.
  • Body and caption hold at 16 and 12 across all three breakpoints. Shrinking body text on a phone costs readability and gains nothing, so only the display sizes reflow.
  • The nav swaps on the two visibility booleans. Bind a layer’s visibility to them instead of hiding layers by hand.
  • Only add a token here if it actually changes at a breakpoint. On a past client project about fifty tokens did the real work in a set of over four hundred, and a wide responsive tier is how a system becomes unmaintainable.
  • Image ratios pair with these breakpoints rather than living here: a 2:1 desktop crop becomes 4:5 on mobile. See the Image System page.
  • The tinted columns are a locked picture of the grid, there so the grid shows in this sheet and in exports. The working grid is the Figma layout grid on the same frame, which you toggle with Ctrl or Cmd plus G. When you duplicate a frame to build in, hide or delete the overlay and keep the layout grid.

Radius

Five steps, and a component picks one by what it is rather than by taste. Controls and cards take radius/sm and radius/md, an overlay or a hero panel takes radius/lg, radius/full belongs to things that are meant to read as a pill, and radius/none is a real choice for a table or a full bleed band rather than the absence of one.

What adjusts automatically

Three different things get called responsive, and Figma automates two of them. Knowing which is which saves a lot of arguing.

Values Automatic

Type sizes, section spacing, grid margins and gutters. Anything bound to a 04 Responsive token resolves from the frame it sits in. Drop a component into the Mobile frame and its type is already mobile type. Nothing to switch.

mechanism: bound tokens plus a pinned mode

Size and reflow Automatic

Width, wrapping and clamping. A component set to fill stretches with its container, auto layout wrap moves items onto new lines as space runs out, and min and max width stop it becoming unusable at either extreme. Field, Select and Card clamp at 480, Accordion at 900, and Nav and Utility Bar never collapse below 320.

mechanism: auto layout fill, wrap, min and max width

Structure Manual

A layout that changes shape rather than scale: a horizontal nav becoming a hamburger, three columns becoming a stack. Figma has no rule that says under 768px use this variant, so someone picks the variant by hand. One exception, below.

mechanism: variants, chosen by hand

The one structural swap that is automatic. Nav / Responsive on the Components page holds both nav layouts at once, each one bound for visibility to visibility/show-desktop-nav and visibility/show-mobile-nav. Because those two booleans are mutually exclusive per mode, the right bar appears on its own from whichever frame it sits in. The three frames above each carry an instance: Desktop shows the full bar, Tablet and Mobile show the hamburger, and nobody picked a variant. Copy this pattern for any component whose layout changes shape between breakpoints. Build both, bind each to a visibility boolean, and let the mode decide. It costs one boolean per breakpoint and removes a manual step permanently.

Illustration

The kit defines the system around illustration, not a house style. Artwork is a commission, and inventing one here would give a client something to inherit that nobody chose.

What the kit does fix is where illustration sits and how it behaves:

  • Sizing. Illustration uses the Image and Aspect Ratio set, so it lands on one of the seven approved ratios rather than on a bespoke box.
  • Placement. Empty State carries the icon slot for the small case. A full illustration belongs in Hero or above a page level empty state, never inside a table body or a menu.
  • Colour. Artwork may use the client's brand ramp and the neutral ramp. It may not use the chart palette, which is spoken for, or the four feedback hues, which mean something.
  • Density. One illustration per screen. A second one on the same view turns both into decoration.
  • When to reach for one. A first run screen, an empty state a user will see more than once, and a marketing band. Not a loading state, which is what Skeleton and Spinner are for, and not an error a user has to read past.

Until a set is commissioned, ship the Empty State icon slot. It is the honest placeholder, and it does not pretend a decision has been made.

Naming

A token name becomes a custom property by swapping slashes for dashes. Tier 3 takes a component prefix so a component decision can never be mistaken for a semantic role:

  • border/focus becomes --border-focus
  • motion/duration/micro becomes --motion-duration-micro
  • button/primary/background becomes --component-button-primary-background

05 Docs has no custom properties. It styles this documentation and the sheets in the Figma file, and it is stripped before a client build.

Working with the tiers

The primitives are scope hidden, so when you pick a colour in Figma you are offered the semantic roles and not the ramp. That is deliberate. If the role you need does not exist, the answer is a new semantic row, not a reach past the layer.

A component decision goes in 03 Component as an alias. If you find yourself typing a hex into a layer, the token that should have existed is the actual missing piece.

Every token, resolved

One sheet per tier, so a dev or an MCP call can be pointed at a single tier instead of the whole wall. Each tier is grouped by family with a count on every group, so you scan headings rather than reading a list. A row shows the swatch where the token is a colour, the token name without its family prefix, what it aliases, and the value that resolves per mode. These sheets hold tokens and nothing else, which is what keeps the export clean.

Tier 2 is three collections. Colour carries Light and Dark, spacing carries Comfortable and Compact, motion carries Full and Reduced, and Figma allows one mode axis per collection, so a tier that needs independent axes has to be split. 06 Icon Library sits outside the tiers: four booleans that choose which drawing every Icon shows. The 27 tokens in 05 Docs are deliberately absent: they style these pages and never ship.

Four booleans, one per library, each true only in its own mode; every Icon variant binds the visibility of its Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor and Remix drawings to them. Apply the mode to a page or a frame the way you switch Light and Dark. No component binds anything else to this collection, and it carries no brand.

For a dev, and for an mcp call

All 543 shipping rows carry a CSS custom property, so a variable defs call returns var(--component-button-primary-background) rather than button/primary/background.

More

The rule is the token path with slashes turned into hyphens, and tier 3 alone takes a component prefix. Nothing needs translating by hand any more.

Point it at a swatch sheet, not a value sheet

The Semantic and Component sheets render swatches bound to their tokens, so a call against either returns that whole tier.

More

The Spacing and Motion sheets print values as text instead, so a call against them returns almost nothing: the Spacing sheet resolves one spacing token. For those two tiers read the rows, or export the collection.

Docs chrome no longer publishes, but still shows up here

All 27 tokens in 05 Docs are now marked hidden from publishing, so a file consuming this library never inherits them.

More

They still resolve on these pages, because hiding only affects consumers. An MCP call is different: it reads this file rather than the library, so a call against any sheet here still returns docs values alongside the kit’s. Filter the docs prefix on anything exported from this file.

Code connect is not set up, and needs a seat

Mapping each component set to its counterpart in code is what makes an MCP call return a real component name and props instead of generic markup.

More

It requires a Dev or Full seat on an Organization or Enterprise plan, so it is a licensing decision rather than a file one. Until then a dev gets correct tokens and hand written markup.

Line height is a lookup, not a binding

Figma cannot bind a proportional line height. A number variable bound to lineHeight is read as pixels, so type/leading/tight at 1.1 becomes a 1.1px line, and forcing the unit back to percent silently drops the binding.

More

That was tested in this file rather than assumed. So the text styles keep percentages and an MCP call returns a bare number. The ratios are still tokenised for code: 1.1 is type/leading/tight, 1.25 is snug, 1.5 is normal. Map the number to the property on the way in, and expect leading/relaxed at 1.65 to be unused headroom.

Components

Components

69 sets, 313 variants on the Components page, in the order of its index. Every one is a real set with real properties, and every visual decision in it is a token. Retail, landing, global and dashboard sets are modules, and live on the Modules page of this site.

DesignerEngineerBoth readingEach set lists the Figma tokens it reads.Each set lists the CSS custom properties it reads.Each set lists its Figma tokens and its CSS custom properties.

Open a set to see the axes as they appear in the properties panel, the text, boolean and instance swap properties, what it composes, and the component tokens it spends. The prose that explains the thinking lives in the Figma description, where you read it while you are using the thing.

Open a set to see its variant axes, its properties, what it composes, and the custom properties it expects to be defined. A set with no component rows of its own is one that should be styled straight from the semantic roles.

Open a set to see its variant axes, its properties, what it composes, and both readings of what it spends: the component tokens a designer binds, and the custom properties an engineer defines. A set with no component rows of its own should be styled straight from the semantic roles. The prose explaining the thinking lives in the Figma description, where you read it while you are using the thing.

DocsFoundationsImage system

Image system

Seven ratios, one component

A small locked family of proportions keeps photography cropping predictably from desktop to mobile. The ratio family came over from a past client system, where it was the most portable thing in the file. Everything after it covers what has to be inside the frame, what happens when text sits on top, how video differs, and what the platform does to an upload.

DesignerEngineerBoth readingThis page reads the same in every reading.

Approved ratios

RatioNameTypical useMobile pair
21:9Ultra-wide heroImmersive full-bleed landing and category banners4:5
2:1Cinematic wideFull-width features, standard page headers4:5
3:2Classic landscapeContent-forward and interactive modules9:16
1:1SquareGrids, tiles, swatches, thumbnails1:1
4:5PortraitHalf-width features; the mobile counterpart4:5
9:16Tall / mobile full-bleedMobile takeovers, vertical story imagery9:16
2:4Full-height portraitFull-height panels, tall product tiles2:4
The rule that matters more than the list. Most modules pair a wider desktop crop with a taller mobile crop of the same content. A 2:1 desktop hero becomes a 4:5 frame on mobile: the subject stays central and the frame changes shape. Art-direct for the pair rather than for one breakpoint, and keep key content inside the centre third, which is the worst case across the three pairs that change shape.

The rule that matters more than the list

Most modules pair a wider desktop crop with a taller mobile crop of the same content. A 2:1 desktop hero becomes a 4:5 frame on mobile: the subject stays central and the frame changes shape. Art-direct for the pair rather than for one breakpoint, and keep key content inside the centre third, which is the worst case across the three pairs that change shape. The next sheet works out each pair exactly.

Before adding an eighth ratio, ask what it buys. The value is in the set staying small.

Lock the ratio on the plate. Image / Aspect Ratio is a fixed plate, not a ratio, so a plate that fills its width while holding a fixed height stops being 1:1 the moment a module is resized. Turn on the aspect ratio lock and the height follows the width, which is the only way an approved ratio survives a band floor.

Which surface takes which crop. The listing tile and the order line at its large size are 4:5, because a product photo is shot portrait. The product page hero and every basket thumbnail are 1:1, because a square is the one crop still legible at 40px, and a gallery thumb has to match the hero it previews. Two crops of the same photo is a real cost to a client, so a project with only one should supply 4:5 and let the square slots crop it.

The safe area is narrower than it looks

The ratio list says what shape an image is. This says what has to be inside it. Everything here is about surviving the desktop to mobile crop, because that is where art direction fails in practice, and the failure is always the same one: the subject was framed for the wide crop.

When the mobile crop is taller than the desktop crop, the mobile frame keeps the full height and loses width. How much width it keeps is just the two ratios divided: the mobile ratio over the desktop ratio. For the three pairs in this family that actually change shape, the answer is between a third and two fifths, which is a good deal less than it feels like.

21:9 becomes 4:5

SAFE

Centre 34.3% survives. Ultra-wide hero to portrait. The narrowest safe area in the set, and the pair most likely to carry a landing banner with a person in it.

2:1 becomes 4:5

SAFE

Centre 40.0% survives. Cinematic wide to portrait. The standard page header pair, so most images in a build go through this one.

3:2 becomes 9:16

SAFE

Centre 37.5% survives. Classic landscape to tall. Content-forward modules, where the subject is usually off centre for compositional reasons and gets cut for exactly that reason.

If you brief one number, brief the centre third. The per pair figures are for checking a specific crop. A photographer needs one instruction, and the safe instruction is the worst case: keep everything that matters inside the centre third of the wide frame. A centre 60 percent rule is the common assumption and it is wrong here, because no pair in this family retains that much.
If you brief one number, brief the centre third. The per pair figures above are for checking a specific crop. A photographer needs one instruction, and the safe instruction is the worst case: keep everything that matters inside the centre third of the wide frame. A centre 60 percent rule is the common assumption and it is wrong here, because no pair in this family retains that much.

Framing by subject

Product on a ground

Centre the product and leave the same proportion of air on all four sides, so the crop pair does not change how big it looks. A product filling the wide frame edge to edge has nowhere to go when the frame narrows. Shoot it smaller than feels right.

People and lifestyle

Faces and hands are what must not be cut, and they are also what sits off centre most often. Keep the face inside the centre third, and leave at least a shoulder width of room below the chin so the tall crop does not cut at the neck.

Detail and texture

The one subject where the crop does not matter, because any part of the frame is as good as any other. Use it for the pairs with the narrowest safe area, and stop trying to art direct a hero out of a product that has no hero shot.

Keeping a shoot consistent

One light direction

Pick a side and hold it for the whole shoot. Images from different sessions end up next to each other in a grid, and mixed light direction is the thing that reads as cheap before anyone can say why.

One ground, or a named set

Either every product sits on the same surface, or the surfaces are a deliberate set of two or three that mean something. Anything in between looks like the shoot ran out of time.

Agree the retouching level

Decide before the shoot how far retouching goes: skin, dust, reflections, background cleanup. A gallery where one image is cleaner than the rest makes the rest look like mistakes.

What never goes into an image

Type

Words baked into a photograph cannot be translated, cannot be read by a screen reader, cannot reflow, and get cut by the crop pair like everything else. Copy goes in a text layer over the image.

Logos and wordmarks

Every reason that applies to type, plus they land at the wrong size on every breakpoint. If a mark has to sit on an image, it is an element of the module rather than part of the photograph.

Anything load bearing near an edge

A price, a badge, a date or a call to action placed in the outer thirds is gone on mobile. If it matters that much, it is a component.

Text over image

Contrast can be computed for a colour and only estimated for a photograph, because the photograph changes. So the rule is not a colour pair, it is a floor: assume the lightest pixel the text could land on and make that pass. The specimens below sit on a synthetic worst case, a ramp running from near black to near white, so every treatment is judged against both ends at once.

No scrim

Everything in its place
One line of supporting copy that still has to be readable.

White text straight onto the photograph. Over the lightest pixel the contrast is 1.12 to 1, which is not a near miss, it is invisible. Only safe when the image is art directed as a dark plate and nobody will ever swap it, which means it is never safe.

Flat scrim, 40 percent

Everything in its place
One line of supporting copy that still has to be readable.

Black at 40 percent over the whole frame. Over the lightest pixel that lands at 3.15 to 1: enough for large display type, short of the 4.5 body text floor. Use it for a single headline, never for a paragraph.

Bottom gradient, 0 to 70 percent

Everything in its place
One line of supporting copy that still has to be readable.

Transparent for the top 45 percent, then down to black at 70 percent. Text sits in the strongest part at 9 to 1, and the image is still legible where it matters. The default for a hero with copy at the bottom.

Solid panel

Everything in its place
One line of supporting copy that still has to be readable.

Copy leaves the photograph entirely and sits on a surface token. Contrast becomes a known quantity again, the text can be any length, and the image is never compromised. Reach for this sooner than feels necessary.

The numbers, worked out

Black scrim over an assumed lightest pixel of F2F2F0, white text on top. These are computed rather than judged by eye, and they are the reason the flat scrim default is 55 percent and not the 40 percent that looks like enough.

ScrimGroundContrastVerdict
0%F2F2F01.12Fails everything. White on a light photograph is not a near miss, it is nothing.
40%9191903.15Large display type only, and only where 3.0 is an acceptable floor. Not for a paragraph.
55%6D6D6C5.18Body text clears AA with room to spare. This is the flat scrim default.
65%5555547.46Clears the 7.0 rule the kit applies to its own primary grounds. Use where the text is the point.
70%4949489.01The bottom stop of the gradient treatment. Past here the photograph stops contributing.

What to use when

One headline, bottom of a hero

The gradient. It keeps the top of the image clean, puts the text in the strongest part, and degrades gracefully if someone swaps the photograph for a lighter one.

A headline and a paragraph

A flat scrim at 55 percent or more. A gradient cannot carry a block of text, because the top line of the block sits in the weak part of the gradient and fails while the bottom line passes.

Anything longer, or any form

A solid panel. Once copy is long enough to reflow unpredictably, or a field or a button is involved, contrast has to be a known quantity and a photograph cannot give you one.

The scrim is a token. The gradient is a spec. A flat scrim binds to image/scrim, new in this version, resolving to black in both light and dark because a scrim sits over content whose luminance nobody controls. Strength stays a layer opacity rather than a token, matching how modal/scrim already works. The gradient cannot be tokenised at all: Figma will only bind a variable to a solid paint, so the two stops are written down and implemented from the same primitive in CSS. That was tested in the file rather than assumed.

Video and motion media

Video enters a page through the same slots as photography and obeys the same ratio family, so most of this is about the two places it does not behave like a still: it has a poster frame that most visitors never get past, and it cannot be reframed after the shoot.

The poster frame is the deliverable

A poster is generated automatically from the video, and automatic is usually wrong, because the first frame of a cut is often a fade from black. Specify the poster as a still, in the same ratio, and treat it as an image in this system. On a slow connection it is the whole design.

Autoplay means muted

Browsers only allow autoplay on a muted video, so an autoplaying video carries no audio information at all. Anything said in it has to exist somewhere else on the page. The platform defaults every playback flag to off, so autoplay is always somebody deciding, never an accident.

Loop length and cut

A decorative loop wants to be under ten seconds with no visible cut at the join. The platform allows ten minutes and a gigabyte, which is far beyond anything decorative. If it is longer than a loop, it is content, and content needs controls.

Decoration or content, not both

Content video needs visible controls, a pause, and captions, and it belongs in the tab order. Decorative video needs none of those and should be unreachable by keyboard. The mistake is designing something in between, which ends up inaccessible and annoying at once.

Reduced motion is not optional

When a visitor has asked for reduced motion, an autoplaying background video shows its poster and does not play. That means the poster has to work as a finished state rather than as a placeholder, which is a second reason to art direct it properly.

Hosted and external are different things

A hosted video renders as a video element and is responsive. An external one renders in an iframe, so it is not responsive, and it arrives with its own controls, its own branding and its own ratio. They look alike in a layout and behave differently in a build, so a module has to say which it takes.

Every video is cropped

Video is shot and exported at 16:9, and 16:9 is not in the approved ratio family. That is deliberate, because the family is built around stills, but it means every video placed in a kit slot loses something. Unlike a photograph, a video cannot be reframed afterwards, so this has to be settled before the shoot rather than in the edit.

FrameLost from a 16:9 masterNote
21:923.8% of the heightCrop top and bottom evenly, and keep nothing important in either quarter. Faces move up the frame fast here.
2:111.1% of the heightThe closest fit in the family, and the one to reach for when a landscape video has to go somewhere.
3:215.6% of the widthCrops more than 2:1 does, despite looking like the safer landscape choice. Worth knowing before defaulting to it.
1:143.8% of the widthOnly for a loop with no subject: texture, fabric, liquid, motion as filler. A person does not survive this.
4:555.0% of the widthExport a portrait master. Cropping a landscape video this hard is not art direction, it is damage.
9:1668.4% of the widthA portrait master, always. There is no version of this that starts from a landscape file.
2:471.9% of the widthPortrait master, and expect to reshoot rather than reframe. The tallest slot in the family.
Brief the video and the poster as one deliverable. The recurring failure is a video shot for 16:9 and a poster grabbed from it afterwards, dropped into a 4:5 mobile slot where more than half the width is gone. Commission the master in the ratio the tallest slot needs, cut the wider frames down from it, and export the poster from the same master at each ratio. It costs nothing at shoot time and cannot be fixed later.

Platform sheet: Shopify

Platform knowledge rather than anything about a client, so it ships with the kit. It applies on top of the approved ratios.

File format

Upload a high quality JPEG or PNG. The CDN negotiates per browser and serves WebP or AVIF where supported, so exporting those by hand gains nothing and costs you the source. PSD, TIFF and BMP upload but get converted. SVG is for logos and icons in theme assets.

Source size

Square product shots at 2048 x 2048. The CDN generates the smaller responsive variants, so do not export each size yourself. Size up rather than down: the CDN will never enlarge an image past its original dimensions.

File size

Stay under 20 MB and 20 megapixels. The docs disagree with themselves here, quoting 25 MP and 5000 x 5000 for product media and 20 MP for online store images, so the smaller pair is the one that is safe everywhere. Aim for under 200 KB after compression.

Compression

Compression runs from your source, so pre-compress before upload. A tidy 300 KB source beats a 4 MB original at the same visible quality. Quality is auto-selected unless the theme sets it; the filter takes 10 to 90 if a large banner is coming out soft.

Responsive delivery

Let the theme image_url and image_tag filters build the srcset. The documented widths depend on the layout: a full width hero takes 600, 900, 1200 and 1600 at 100vw, a two column grid takes 300 to 800, a four column grid takes 200 to 600. Always emit width and height so nothing shifts.

Focal point

Set it where the image is chosen in the theme editor. It is a CSS object-position value, not a server side crop, and it only reaches the page through the image_tag filter. Hand rolled markup built from image_url alone drops it silently, which is worth saying out loud at handoff.

Alt text

Fill the alt text field on every media item. Leave it empty for purely decorative images so screen readers skip them.

Lazy loading

The image_tag filter already decides this by section position, eager for the first three sections and lazy from the fourth. Do not override it without a reason. The one addition worth making is fetchpriority high on the above the fold image, which is usually the first banner or the PDP shot.

The transform filter

Everything the platform can do to an image happens in image_url: width and height up to 5760, crop as top, center, bottom, left, right or an explicit region, quality from 10 to 90. Format conversion only goes to jpg or progressive jpg. There is no WebP parameter, because that is a delivery decision rather than a filter one.

Media types

A product carries four kinds of media: image, hosted video, external video from YouTube or Vimeo, and 3D model. Two hundred and fifty items per product, which no design will reach. Each type renders through its own tag, so a gallery that mixes them is four code paths, not one.

Three places an image can live

Product media sits on the product. Files under Content is for everything a section or a metafield points at. Theme assets is for chrome that ships with the theme, like a logo. The limits differ per place, and so does who can change the image later, which is usually the deciding factor.

Variant images

One image per variant, and that is a platform limit rather than a theme one. A variant that needs three shots uses the product gallery for the other two, so design the gallery to carry them rather than expecting the picker to.

What bites you on this platform

Six behaviours that are documented but easy to miss, each of which has cost somebody a day. The first two are the ones to read before your next export.

Nothing gets enlarged

The platform will never resize an image above its original dimensions. Ask for 3000 wide from a 1200 wide source and you get 1200, quietly. It also means a srcset listing nine widths can resolve to three real files, so a hero that looks soft on a large screen is usually a source problem rather than a compression one.

Colour profiles are stripped

ICC and ICM profiles are removed on the way to the storefront and sRGB is assumed. Anything authored in Adobe RGB or Display P3 shifts, usually desaturating, and no theme setting can bring it back. Export sRGB and strip the profile before upload. This is the highest value item here and the least known.

An SVG will not crop

The platform cannot resize or crop an SVG unless you also ask for a raster format back, at which point it is not an SVG any more. Keep vector for chrome that is used at one size, and never route it through a section that crops.

Transparency dies on conversion

The only format conversions available are jpg and progressive jpg, and neither has an alpha channel. A transparent PNG forced to jpg comes back with a background behind it. When a ratio mismatch needs filling, the pad colour parameter is the intended answer.

Animated GIFs are a maybe

Animated GIFs are converted to animated WebP at delivery, which is a straight saving. What is not documented is what a transform does to one. Since the only format targets are still images, assume the animation is lost and test before routing a GIF through a cropping section.

Aspect ratio has hard bounds

Uploads are rejected outside 100:1 and 1:100. That sounds generous until someone exports a full width ribbon strip or a very tall size chart as one image. Split it, or carry it as two.

Platform sheet: another platform

Duplicate this sheet for a new platform and fill it in. Do not edit the Shopify sheet to fit a different stack.

TopicQuestion to answer
File formatWhat does this platform serve, and what should be uploaded?
Source sizeRecommended source dimensions, and whether variants are generated.
File sizeHard limits, and the practical target after compression.
Responsive deliveryHow does the srcset get built: framework, CDN, or by hand?
Focal pointIs there a focal-point control, or does art direction have to handle cropping?
AccessibilityWhere does alt text live, and what marks an image decorative?
PerformanceLazy-loading approach and how the LCP image is prioritised.
GotchasAnything that cost someone a day on this platform.

Client photography

A retoned template full of grey ratio plates still does not look like the client. Their own photos do, so step 9 of the adaptation prompt migrates them. The rules that matter here:

Originals, not screenshots

The connector cannot copy an image fill between files, so each photo is downloaded from the client file, hashed with SHA-1, which is Figma’s own image hash, and uploaded into the kit copy. The hash keeps every photo traceable to its source and drops duplicates.

One library sheet

A Client imagery sheet on this page, grouped by the client page each photo came from, split into product shots and lifestyle photos, each tile captioned with its nearest kit ratio.

Photos only fill the image component

Every Image / Aspect Ratio instance gets a photo as an instance fill override, labels off. Never an image fill on a frame or a card, and the main component never changes: it keeps documenting the ratios.

The full procedure is step 9 of the adaptation prompt, on the Client adaptation page. The kit itself ships no client photography: every plate is a ratio plate.

What stays with the project

Which module uses which ratio is client-specific and stays with the project. This page holds the ratio family, the safe areas, the art direction rules, the legibility floors and the platform sheets. The method travels; the application does not.

Interactions and motion

Interactions and motion

Twenty four behaviours, each answering the same six questions and each carrying the block a coding agent reads, with a live demo running on the kit motion tokens. Anything a static frame cannot show belongs here. Motion is a token tier, so reduced motion is a mode rather than an afterthought.

DesignerEngineerBoth readingThe six answers and a live demo for every entry.Adds the coding agent prompt, with a Copy button, to all 24 entries.The six answers, the live demo and the coding agent prompt.

The motion tier

Two modes, and the distinction between them is the useful part. Transitions collapse. Waits hold. Curves are untouched.

Collapsing a wait would break the thing it protects. A toast whose dwell went to zero would vanish before it could be read, and a tooltip whose intent delay went to zero would trail a line of labels behind the pointer across the screen. So motion/duration/intent and motion/duration/dwell hold their values in Reduced, and everything that describes a transition goes to 0.

One caveat worth knowing: nothing in Figma can bind a duration. The curves are string variables and they do bind, but a duration in the Figma file is named in prose next to the frame. The token layer is the only place a duration is real, which is exactly why an engineer should never type one.

Motion sheet in Figma  ·  Global rules sheet

Six questions, five rules

Every entry answers six things

  1. What it does: in one sentence, from the user’s side of the screen.
  2. What triggers it: hover, click, scroll position, time, focus, page load.
  3. Timing and easing: duration in ms and the curve. Name the token if there is one.
  4. What it does on mobile, and whether the trigger even exists there.
  5. What it does with prefers-reduced-motion set.
  6. What a keyboard user experiences: what is focusable, in what order.

Copy the spec template frame for each behaviour you spec. An entry that cannot answer all six is unfinished, and the two that get skipped most are reduced motion and the keyboard path.

True for every interaction in the system

  • Every motion has a reduced-motion answer. “Nothing happens” is a valid answer; “unspecified” is not.
  • Focus is always visible. The focus ring is bound to border/focus and clears 3:1 against the page surface.
  • Hover is never the only route to content or an action.
  • Touch targets are at least 44 x 44, whatever the visual size of the control.
  • Anything that moves on a timer can be paused, by pointer and by keyboard.

01Accessibility

Focus ring

The ring that tells a keyboard user where they are. Every focusable control has one, and it is never removed without a replacement.

Text link
Live demoPress Tab inside the frame, or Play to walk the ring across the controls. A mouse click leaves no ring.
Trigger
Keyboard focus, not pointer click
Timing
focus/duration, standard curve
Mobile
Present for external keyboards
Reduced
Ring still appears, no transition
Keyboard
Tab in DOM order, never trapped outside a modal
Applies to
Every interactive set
Prompt for a coding agent 
Focus ring

Build
  Draw a 2px ring outside the control using outline with an offset, so it never changes layout. Show it on :focus-visible only, so a mouse click does not leave a ring behind.

Tokens
  --component-focus-duration        75ms                          → motion/duration/micro
  --motion-ease-standard            cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)    → ease/standard
  --border-focus                    #5E6D82                       → color/brand/500

CSS
  :focus-visible {
    outline: 2px solid var(--border-focus);
    outline-offset: 2px;
    transition: outline-color var(--component-focus-duration) var(--motion-ease-standard);
  }

Reduced motion
  The ring still appears at full strength. Only the colour transition is dropped.

Keyboard
  Tab reaches every control in DOM order. Focus is never trapped except inside an open modal or drawer, and never removed with outline: none.

Mobile
  Not triggered by touch, but it has to work for external keyboards and switch control.

02Action

Button hover and press

The colour change that confirms a button is live under the pointer, and the press that confirms the click landed.

Live demoHover the button. The ground changes in 75ms and nothing moves.
Trigger
Pointer hover, then active
Timing
button/duration, standard curve
Mobile
No hover exists, nothing may depend on it
Reduced
Colour changes with no transition
Keyboard
Focus and hover are separate states
Applies to
Button, Icon Button, Link
Prompt for a coding agent 
Button hover and press

Build
  Transition background-color and border-color only. Do not move the button, do not scale it and do not animate a shadow: a 2px lift on a 44px target is the difference between a click and a miss.

Tokens
  --component-button-duration       75ms                          → motion/duration/micro
  --motion-ease-standard            cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)    → ease/standard
  --component-button-primary-background #4D596A                       → action/primary
  --component-button-primary-background-hover #3E4856                       → action/primary-hover

CSS
  .button {
    transition-property: background-color, border-color;
    transition-duration: var(--component-button-duration);
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-standard);
  }
  .button:hover {
    background-color: var(--component-button-primary-background-hover);
  }

Reduced motion
  The colour still changes. Only the transition is dropped.

Keyboard
  Hover and focus are separate. A focused button that is not hovered shows the ring, not the hover ground.

Mobile
  There is no hover on touch. The kit ships Default, Hover and Disabled; a pressed state is project work and belongs in 03 Component as button/primary/background-active rather than a darken in CSS.

Build
  Change the row background only. Cells are transparent by design, so the fill runs the full width with nothing showing through between columns. Do not transition the row rule.

Tokens
  --component-row-duration          75ms                          → motion/duration/micro
  --motion-ease-standard            cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)    → ease/standard

  --component-table-row-hover       #F2F2F3                       → surface/muted

  The ground still changes. Only the transition is dropped.

Tooltip reveal

A label that appears after the pointer rests, and disappears the moment it leaves.

Shipping estimateBased on the warehouse nearest you
Live demoRest the pointer on the icon: 300ms of intent, then a 150ms rise. Keyboard focus shows it at once and Escape hides it.
Trigger
Pointer rest, or keyboard focus
Timing
tooltip/delay then tooltip/duration
Mobile
Never appears, so it can hold nothing essential
Reduced
No rise, no fade, same delay
Keyboard
Focus shows it at once, Escape dismisses
Applies to
Tooltip
Prompt for a coding agent 
Tooltip reveal

Build
  Wait the delay before showing, so crossing the screen does not flash a trail of tooltips. Fade in and rise 4px. On exit go immediately, with no delay, on the exit curve.

Tokens
  --component-tooltip-delay         300ms                         → motion/duration/intent
  --component-tooltip-duration      150ms                         → motion/duration/fast
  --motion-ease-entrance            cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)    → ease/decelerate
  --motion-ease-exit                cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)    → ease/accelerate

CSS
  .tooltip {
    transition-property: opacity, transform;
    transition-duration: var(--component-tooltip-duration);
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-entrance);
    transition-delay: var(--component-tooltip-delay);
  }
  .tooltip[data-state=closed] {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateY(4px);
    transition-delay: 0ms;
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-exit);
  }

Reduced motion
  No rise and no fade. It appears and disappears, still after the delay.

Keyboard
  Focus shows it immediately with no delay, and Escape dismisses it. It is wired with aria-describedby on the control it labels.

Mobile
  There is no hover, so the tooltip never appears. Anything it says has to exist somewhere a touch user can reach.

Prompt for a coding agent 
Modal open and close

Build
  Fade the scrim and scale the panel from 0.98 to 1 at the same time and over the same duration. On close, run both on the exit curve. Lock scrolling behind it.

Tokens
  --component-modal-duration        300ms                         → motion/duration/slow
  --motion-ease-entrance            cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)    → ease/decelerate
  --motion-ease-exit                cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)    → ease/accelerate
  --component-modal-scrim           #3A3D40                       → surface/overlay

CSS
  .modal-scrim,
  .modal-panel {
    transition-duration: var(--component-modal-duration);
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-entrance);
  }
  .modal-scrim { transition-property: opacity; }
  .modal-panel { transition-property: opacity, transform; }
  [data-state=closed] .modal-panel {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: scale(0.98);
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-exit);
  }

Reduced motion
  Scrim and panel appear with no transform and no transition. The scroll lock is unaffected.

Keyboard
  Focus moves to the panel on open, Tab cycles inside it, Escape closes, and focus returns to the trigger. This is the one place focus is deliberately trapped.

Mobile
  Full width with a top inset. Drop the scale below 640px: a panel that fills the screen has nothing to scale against.

11Loading

Skeleton to content

The shimmer that says the page is working, and the swap when it is not needed any more.

AW
A. Wilson

Approved the autumn capsule and left two notes on the tote.

Live demoPlay a load. The shimmer loops at 1200ms, then the content swaps in over 200ms.
Trigger
A request starting, then resolving
Timing
skeleton/loop for the shimmer, base for the swap
Mobile
Identical
Reduced
No shimmer at all, static block
Keyboard
aria-busy while loading, focus does not move
Applies to
Skeleton
Prompt for a coding agent 
Skeleton to content

Build
  Move a gradient across the skeleton on a loop. When the data arrives, crossfade the skeleton out and the content in over the base duration. Match the skeleton to the shape of what it stands in for, or the swap will jump.

Tokens
  --component-skeleton-loop         1200ms                        → motion/duration/loop
  --motion-ease-loop                cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)      → ease/linear
  --motion-duration-base            200ms                         → duration/200
  --motion-ease-standard            cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)    → ease/standard
  --component-skeleton-base         #F2F2F3                       → surface/muted

CSS
  @keyframes shimmer {
    to { background-position-x: -200%; }
  }
  .skeleton {
    animation: shimmer var(--component-skeleton-loop)
               var(--motion-ease-loop) infinite;
  }
  .content {
    transition: opacity var(--motion-duration-base)
                var(--motion-ease-standard);
  }

Reduced motion
  No shimmer. The skeleton is a static block and the swap is instant. A permanent loop is exactly what reduced motion is asking you to remove.

Keyboard
  The region carries aria-busy while it loads. Focus does not move when the content arrives, so a keyboard user is not thrown out of position.

Mobile
  Identical. The shimmer is cheap enough on mobile, but drop it entirely if the device reports reduced motion or a save-data preference.

Progress

Mobile
Identical
Reduced
Determinate jumps, indeterminate is replaced

role progressbar with aria-valuenow
Applies to
Progress, Spinner
Prompt for a coding agent 
Progress

Build
  Transition width for a determinate bar. For indeterminate, translate a fixed-width fill across the track on a loop, on the loop curve so it does not appear to hesitate at each end.

Tokens
  --component-progress-duration     200ms                         → motion/duration/base
  --motion-ease-standard            cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)    → ease/standard
  --motion-duration-loop            1200ms                        → duration/1200
  --motion-ease-loop                cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)      → ease/linear
  --component-progress-fill         #4D596A                       → action/primary

CSS
  .progress-fill {
    transition: width var(--component-progress-duration)
                var(--motion-ease-standard);
  }
  .progress-fill[data-indeterminate] {
    width: 40%;
    animation: slide var(--motion-duration-loop)
               var(--motion-ease-loop) infinite;
  }

Reduced motion
  A determinate bar updates with no transition. An indeterminate one should be replaced with a static bar or a text status, since a permanent loop is the thing reduced motion exists to stop.

Keyboard
  role progressbar with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax. For indeterminate, drop aria-valuenow and mark the region aria-busy.

Mobile
  Identical. Keep the track at least 4px so it stays visible on a dense screen.

13Feedback

Button multi-state feedback

A button that does work has to say so. Idle, pending, then settled, without the layout moving underneath it.

Live demoSubmit. Pending in 150ms, the settled state holds for the dwell, then back in 200ms. The width never changes.
Trigger
Submit or activation, never hover
Timing
motion/duration/fast in, motion/duration/dwell on the settled state, motion/duration/base out
Mobile
Identical. The width is reserved up front so no row reflows.
Reduced
States still change. The spinner stops spinning and the label swaps without a morph.
Keyboard
Focus stays on the button throughout. aria-busy while pending, and the result announced in a live region.
Applies to
Button, Icon Button
Prompt for a coding agent 
Button multi-state feedback

Build
  One button, four states: idle, pending, success, error. Reserve the width of the
  longest label before the first render, so a state change never reflows the row it
  sits in. The pending state disables activation but keeps focus.

Tokens
  --motion-duration-fast            150ms                         → duration/150
  --motion-duration-base            200ms                         → duration/200
  --motion-duration-dwell           5000ms                        → duration/5000
  --motion-ease-standard            cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)    → ease/standard
  --component-button-primary-background   #4D596A                 → color/brand/500
  --feedback-success                                              → semantic role
  --feedback-error                                                → semantic role

CSS
  .btn { min-width: var(--reserved); transition:
         background-color var(--motion-duration-fast) var(--motion-ease-standard); }
  .btn[data-state="pending"] { pointer-events: none; }
  .btn[data-state="success"] { background: var(--feedback-success); }

Sequence
  idle → pending        on activation, immediately, no delay
  pending → success     when the request resolves, not on a timer
  success → idle        after dwell, unless the view has navigated away
  pending → error       on failure, and it stays until dismissed or retried

Reduced motion
  Every state still renders. The spinner becomes a static indicator and the label
  crossfade becomes an instant swap.

Keyboard
  Focus never moves. Set aria-busy on the button while pending and announce the
  outcome in a polite live region, because a colour change is not an announcement.

Mobile
  Same behaviour. Do not shrink the hit area in the pending state.

14Destructive

Hold to confirm

Confirmation for a destructive action without putting a modal in the way. The user holds, a fill runs, and letting go early cancels it.

Live demoPress and hold, or hold Space. Let go early and nothing happens. The fill is linear because it is progress.
Trigger
Pointer down, or Space held. Never a click.
Timing
motion/duration/hold at 600ms, linear curve
Mobile
Long press, same duration. Suppress the native context menu.
Reduced
The fill still runs. It is progress, not decoration, so it is never removed.
Keyboard
Space held to arm, release to cancel, Escape to cancel. The action fires on completion, not on keyup.
Applies to
Destructive actions where a modal would be disproportionate
Prompt for a coding agent 
Hold to confirm

Build
  A destructive control that arms on press and fires only when a 600ms fill
  completes. Releasing early cancels and returns the fill to zero. The label states
  what will happen, so the control reads as Hold to delete rather than Delete.

Tokens
  --motion-duration-hold            600ms                         → duration/600
  --motion-ease-linear              cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)      → ease/linear
  --motion-duration-fast            150ms                         → duration/150
  --component-button-destructive-background   #79302A             → feedback/error

CSS
  .hold::after { transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left;
                 transition: transform var(--motion-duration-hold) var(--motion-ease-linear); }
  .hold[data-armed="true"]::after { transform: scaleX(1); }
  /* cancel returns in fast, not hold, so releasing feels immediate */
  .hold:not([data-armed="true"])::after { transition-duration: var(--motion-duration-fast); }

Why linear
  The fill is a progress indicator, and an eased fill lies about how much time is
  left. Use linear here even though the rest of the system does not.

Reduced motion
  Kept in full. Removing it would remove the only signal that the action is
  underway and the only window in which to cancel.

Keyboard
  Space arms on keydown and cancels on keyup before completion. Escape cancels.
  Announce the armed state, because a silent fill is invisible to a screen reader.

Mobile
  Long press with the same 600ms. Call preventDefault on contextmenu so the OS
  menu does not interrupt the hold.

15Entrance

Scroll reveal and stagger

Content that arrives as it comes into view, once, and never at the cost of being readable before it does.

Made to last
Repairable
Shipped free
Thirty day returns
Live demoReplay it. Each tile rises 16px over 200ms, 75ms after the one before. It fires once on scroll in.
Trigger
Twenty percent of the element in view. Fires once and never again.
Timing
motion/duration/base, decelerate curve, motion/stagger/base between siblings
Mobile
Same, but cap the total stagger. Eight items at 150ms is 1.2 seconds of waiting.
Reduced
No transform and no stagger. Content is simply present at full opacity.
Keyboard
Content is in the DOM, focusable and readable before it animates. Tabbing ahead never lands on something invisible.
Applies to
Feature Row, Stat Strip, Media and Copy, any module that lists siblings
Prompt for a coding agent 
Scroll reveal and stagger

Build
  Reveal on first entry into the viewport using IntersectionObserver at a 0.2
  threshold, then unobserve. Siblings offset by one stagger step. Travel is 16px,
  which is space/16, so the movement sits on the spacing scale rather than being a
  number somebody picked.

Tokens
  --motion-duration-base            200ms                         → duration/200
  --motion-stagger-base             75ms                          → duration/75
  --motion-stagger-loose            150ms                         → duration/150
  --motion-ease-entrance            cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)    → ease/decelerate
  travel                            16px                          → space/16

CSS
  .reveal { opacity: 1; }                      /* the resting state is visible */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
    .reveal { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(16px);
              transition: opacity var(--motion-duration-base) var(--motion-ease-entrance),
                          transform var(--motion-duration-base) var(--motion-ease-entrance);
              transition-delay: calc(var(--i, 0) * var(--motion-stagger-base)); }
    .reveal[data-in="true"] { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
  }

The cap
  Total stagger never exceeds 400ms. Past that the last item reads as broken rather
  than as choreographed. With more than five siblings, switch from per-item stagger
  to revealing the group as one block.

Once only
  Unobserve after the first entry. Re-animating on scroll back is the most common
  way this pattern turns from pleasant into irritating.

Reduced motion
  No transform, no opacity change, no delay. Note the CSS above: the visible state
  is the default and the animation is added inside the media query, so a reduced
  preference cannot leave content stuck at zero opacity.

Keyboard
  Never gate content on scroll position. The element is present and focusable from
  first paint; only its opacity and transform are animated.

Mobile
  Same threshold. Watch the cap, because a phone viewport shows fewer siblings at
  once and the stagger is more noticeable.
