16Navigation

Page transition

The change between two routes, and the focus move that most implementations forget.

LOGO

Home

Live demoSwitch page. The old view leaves in 150ms, the new one arrives in 200ms, and focus moves to its heading.
Trigger
Route change, after the incoming view is ready to paint
Timing
motion/duration/fast out, motion/duration/base in, accelerate then decelerate
Mobile
Same, and it must never block the system back gesture
Reduced
Crossfade only, no movement. The route still changes at the same speed.
Keyboard
Focus moves to the incoming view heading and the change is announced. Without this a screen reader stays on the old page.
Applies to
Templates
Prompt for a coding agent 
Page transition

Build
  Exit the outgoing view, then enter the incoming one. Do not overlap them for
  longer than the exit, or both routes are on screen and neither reads as current.
  Hold the scroll position of the outgoing view until it has left.

Tokens
  --motion-duration-fast            150ms                         → duration/150
  --motion-duration-base            200ms                         → duration/200
  --motion-ease-exit                cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)    → ease/accelerate
  --motion-ease-entrance            cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)    → ease/decelerate

Sequence
  out       150ms   opacity to 0, translateY -8px, accelerate
  in        200ms   opacity to 1, translateY from 8px, decelerate
  focus     on entry complete, move focus to the h1 of the incoming view
  announce  set the document title, then announce the route in a live region

CSS
  View transitions where supported, with a transition-name on the shell only.
  Do not name every element: a transition that tries to morph a whole page costs
  more than it returns and breaks the moment the two routes differ structurally.

Reduced motion
  Crossfade with no translate. Keep the same total duration, because shortening it
  makes the route change feel like a failure rather than a preference.

Keyboard
  This is the part that gets skipped. On completion, move focus to the incoming
  heading with tabindex="-1", update document.title, and announce in a polite live
  region. A transition that animates beautifully and leaves focus on a button that
  no longer exists is worse than no transition.

Mobile
  Never intercept the back gesture. If the platform owns the transition, let it,
  and keep only the focus move and the announcement.

17Data

List add and remove

A row arriving in a list, or leaving it, and the rows below closing the gap behind it. The motion is the easy half.

  • Linen
  • Canvas
  • Leather
Live demoAdd a row, or remove one. The row fades in 150ms, then the gap closes over 200ms, and focus moves to the next row.
Trigger
A row added or removed, by the person or by an update arriving.
Timing
motion/duration/fast for the row itself, motion/duration/base for the gap closing. Entrance curve in, exit curve out.
Mobile
Identical. Swipe to remove is a second way to reach it, never the only one.
Reduced
No fade, no shift, no collapse. Focus and the announcement are unaffected: neither is motion.
Keyboard
Focus moves to the next row, or the previous one if it was last. Never to the body.
Applies to
List Row, Table Row, File Row, removable Tag, any stack a person edits
Prompt for a coding agent 
List add and remove

Build
  Animate two things on different clocks. The row fades and shifts 8px on the fast
  duration; the gap it leaves closes on the base duration, so the list settles just
  after the row has gone rather than at the same moment. Animate grid-template-rows
  from 1fr to 0fr, or height from the measured value. Never to a hardcoded height.

  Remove the node from the DOM on transitionend, not on click. Removing it first
  means a screen reader can be mid-sentence on a row that no longer exists.

Tokens
  --motion-duration-fast            150ms                         → motion/duration/fast
  --motion-duration-base            200ms                         → motion/duration/base
  --motion-ease-entrance            cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)    → ease/decelerate
  --motion-ease-exit                cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)    → ease/accelerate
  travel                            8px                           → space/8

CSS
  .list-row {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-rows: 1fr;
    transition: grid-template-rows var(--motion-duration-base)
                var(--motion-ease-exit);
  }
  .list-row > .inner {
    overflow: hidden;
    transition: opacity   var(--motion-duration-fast) var(--motion-ease-exit),
                transform var(--motion-duration-fast) var(--motion-ease-exit);
  }
  .list-row[data-state="leaving"] { grid-template-rows: 0fr; }
  .list-row[data-state="leaving"] > .inner {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateY(-8px);
  }
  .list-row[data-state="entering"] > .inner {
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-entrance);
  }

Focus, on removal
  Decide where focus goes before the row leaves: the next row, or the previous one
  if the removed row was last, or the list container if it is now empty. Focus must
  never fall to the body. A keyboard user who deletes the third of twelve rows and
  lands back at the top of the page has to find their place again every time.

Announcement
  The list owns one aria-live="polite" region, and it says what happened and what is
  left: "Invoice 0412 removed, 11 remaining". Not "removed", which drops the number
  that was the reason to look.

Reduced motion
  No fade, no shift, no collapse. The row is there or it is not and the list reflows
  instantly. The focus move and the announcement still happen, because neither of
  them is motion.

Mobile
  Identical. If a project adds swipe to remove, the swipe reaches the same removal
  and ends in the same animation, and a visible control does the same job for anyone
  who cannot swipe.

What not to do
  Do not animate the whole list. Moving every row on every change costs a layout pass
  per frame and makes a ten row list feel heavier than a hundred row table. Only the
  row that changed animates; the rest are moved by the gap closing.

The tooltip is a convenience, not the data. If the only way to read a value is to hover the right pixel, the chart fails keyboard, touch and screen reader users at once. Ship the numbers in text beside the chart or in a table behind it, then let the tooltip make them faster to find.
Prompt for a coding agent 
Chart hover and tooltip

Build
  Snap to the nearest category, not the exact pointer x. Draw the cursor line at that
  category, keep its marks at full strength and drop the rest to 35%, then place the
  Chart Tooltip beside the cursor on the side with more room. No delay: unlike a control
  tooltip, someone reading a chart is already looking for the value.

  The tooltip repeats what the chart shows. Every value it holds also exists in a data
  table or a visually hidden summary, so the chart is never the only way to a number.

Tokens
  --component-tooltip-duration      150ms                         → motion/duration/fast
  --component-row-duration          75ms                          → motion/duration/micro
  --motion-ease-entrance            cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)    → ease/decelerate
  --motion-ease-standard            cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)    → ease/standard
  --chart-axis                      #C7C9CC                       → color/neutral/300

CSS
  .chart-mark {
    transition: opacity var(--component-row-duration) var(--motion-ease-standard);
  }
  .chart[data-active] .chart-mark:not([data-active]) { opacity: 0.35; }
  .chart-tooltip {
    transition-property: opacity, transform;
    transition-duration: var(--component-tooltip-duration);
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-entrance);
  }
  .chart-tooltip[data-state=closed] { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(4px); }
  .chart-cursor { stroke: var(--chart-axis); stroke-width: 1px; }

Keyboard
  The plot is one tab stop with role="group" and a label that names the chart. Left and
  Right step through categories, Up and Down through series where there is more than
  one, Home and End jump to the ends. The focused point drives the same tooltip, and its
  text goes to an aria-live="polite" region: "March, Desktop 237, Mobile 120".

Reduced motion
  The dim and the card appear and disappear with no transition. The cursor still follows
  the pointer, because it tracks input rather than animating.

Mobile
  No hover. A tap on a mark pins its tooltip, a tap on another mark moves it, and a tap
  outside the plot clears it. Never open a tooltip on scroll.

Trigger

Timing
motion/duration/slow per slide, motion/duration/dwell between auto-advances
Mobile

Native scroll does most of the work. A transform-driven track has to rebuild swipe, momentum, trackpad, snapping and focus scrolling, and it usually gets one of them wrong. scroll-snap gets all of them from the browser. Reach for a library only when the design needs a loop.
Prompt for a coding agent 
Carousel

Build
  Use native horizontal scroll with scroll-snap and drive it from the arrows with
  scrollBy, rather than a transform track. Native scroll gives swipe, momentum and
  trackpad for free. Move by one slide per press, or one page when several are visible.
  Where a project animates the track itself, use the slow duration on the standard curve.

  Autoplay is off by default. If a project turns it on, advance after the dwell and pause
  on hover, on focus within the carousel and while the tab is hidden, and show a visible
  pause control. Hover alone strands keyboard and touch users.

Tokens
  --motion-duration-slow            300ms                         → duration/300
  --motion-duration-dwell           5000ms                        → duration/5000
  --motion-ease-standard            cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)    → ease/standard

CSS
  .carousel-track {
    display: flex;
    overflow-x: auto;
    scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;
    scroll-behavior: smooth;
  }
  .carousel-slide { flex: 0 0 auto; scroll-snap-align: start; }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .carousel-track { scroll-behavior: auto; }
  }

Indicator
  Carousel Indicator dots are status, not controls, unless the project gives each one a
  44px target and a focus state. Pick one and spec it: a dot that looks tappable and is
  not is the first worked example on this page.

Keyboard
  Previous and Next are real buttons labelled for what they do, and they disable at the
  ends unless the carousel loops. The track carries aria-roledescription="carousel" and
  each slide is labelled "2 of 6". With autoplay running the live region is off, or it
  reads every advance aloud.

Reduced motion
  Slides change with no travel and autoplay does not start. Arrows and swipe still work.

Mobile
  Swipe is the primary control. Below 640 the arrows hide and the dots remain as status.
  Let the next slide peek so the row reads as scrollable.

Trigger

Timing

Mobile

Reduced

Mega Menu, Store Navbar, Nav Drawer, Site Header, Mobile Menu
Hover to open is the expensive part. A menu that opens on hover needs the intent wait, a diagonal path that does not close it, a grace period on leave and a click fallback, and it still misbehaves on touch laptops. Click to open is the default for that reason. Hover is a project decision, made knowingly.
Prompt for a coding agent 
Mega menu and nav drawer

Build
  The top-level item is a button with aria-expanded, not a link that also opens a menu.
  Click toggles the panel. If a project adds hover to open, wait the intent duration
  first, keep the panel open while the pointer travels diagonally toward it, and close
  after a short grace period once the pointer has left both, never instantly.

  One panel at a time. Opening a second closes the first with no exit animation, so
  moving along the bar reads as switching rather than a stack of fades.

Tokens
  --motion-duration-intent          300ms                         → duration/300
  --component-menu-duration         150ms                         → motion/duration/fast
  --component-drawer-duration       300ms                         → motion/duration/slow
  --motion-ease-entrance            cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)    → ease/decelerate
  --motion-ease-exit                cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)    → ease/accelerate

CSS
  .mega-panel {
    transition-property: opacity, transform;
    transition-duration: var(--component-menu-duration);
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-entrance);
  }
  .mega-panel[data-state=closed] {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateY(-4px);
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-exit);
  }
  .nav-drawer {
    transition: transform var(--component-drawer-duration) var(--motion-ease-entrance);
  }
  .nav-drawer[data-state=closed] { transform: translateX(-100%); }

Keyboard
  Tab moves along the bar. Enter, Space or Down opens a panel and moves focus to its
  first link, and Tab walks the links in reading order. Escape closes the panel and
  returns focus to its button. Do not use role="menu": site navigation is a list of links.

Reduced motion
  The panel and the drawer appear and disappear in place. The intent wait stays, because
  it is a wait rather than motion.

Mobile
  No mega panel. The Nav Drawer slides from the left on the drawer duration with the same
  focus trap as Drawer, and each top-level section is an accordion inside it.

21Commerce

Add to bag

The one action a storefront is measured on. Press, pending, settled, and a bag count that changes where someone can see it.

LOGO0
Canvas weekender bag

£148

Live demoAdd to bag. The count changes only when the server confirms, with the flight and a small tick.
Trigger
Activation of the add control. Never hover, and never a second time while pending.
Timing
Button states per the multi-state spec. The count changes the moment the server confirms, not on press.
Mobile
Identical, and the sticky buy bar carries the same button in the same state.
Reduced
Every state still changes. The count still updates. Only the flight and the count tick are dropped.
Keyboard
Focus stays on the button. aria-busy while pending, and the result announced in a live region.
Applies to
Product Tile, Quickview, the PDP buy column, the sticky buy bar
Prompt for a coding agent 
Add to bag

Build
  Three things happen and only one of them is decoration.

  1. The button runs the multi-state sequence: idle, pending, settled. Reserve the
     width of the longest label first, so a product tile does not reflow its grid
     row when one tile goes to Working.
  2. The bag count updates when the server confirms, never optimistically on press.
     A count that goes up and then back down is worse than a count that waits.
  3. Optionally, the product image travels to the bag. This is the decoration.

Tokens
  --component-button-duration       75ms                          → motion/duration/micro
  --motion-duration-fast            150ms                         → motion/duration/fast
  --motion-duration-base            200ms                         → motion/duration/base
  --motion-duration-dwell           5000ms                        → motion/duration/dwell
  --motion-ease-standard            cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)    → ease/standard
  --motion-ease-spring              cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.4, 0.64, 1) → ease/overshoot
  --component-button-success-background                           → feedback/success-subtle

Sequence
  press       0ms      state to Pending, aria-busy true, activation blocked
  confirm     server   state to Success, bag count increments, live region speaks
  settle      5000ms   state back to Idle. The count stays where it is.

Announcement
  One polite live region, and it names the thing and the total:
  "Ridgeline kettle added, 3 items in your bag". Not "added to bag", which makes
  someone open the bag to find out what happened.

The count
  The number on the bag is the only part of this that persists. Give it its own
  small scale animation on the overshoot curve, 150ms, and nothing else. Do not
  animate the bag icon itself: a moving target is harder to read than a still one
  with a changing number.

The flight, if you want it
  Clone the product image, position the clone with getBoundingClientRect over the
  original, then transform it to the bag rect. Animate transform and opacity only,
  never top and left, or every frame costs a layout. Remove the clone on finish.

  It must survive being deleted. The add is complete whether or not the flight ran,
  the count updates independently of it, and a sticky header that moves mid-flight
  is allowed to make it land in the wrong place, because nothing depends on where
  it lands.

Reduced motion
  No flight, no count tick. The states still change and the count still updates,
  because both are information. Removing them would remove the confirmation.

Errors
  Out of stock and a failed request are different. Out of stock disables the button
  and says so next to it; the request failing shows the Error state and leaves the
  button pressable. Do not use a Toast for either: the answer belongs beside the
  control the person just used.

Prompt for a coding agent 
Cart drawer and mini cart

Build
  Open the drawer only after the add succeeds, never optimistically. While the request
  runs the button shows its pending state (entry 13). On success update the header
  count, then slide the Cart Drawer in from the right on the drawer duration. On failure
  the drawer stays shut and the button shows the error.

  The Mini Cart is the lighter option: a panel under the cart control on the menu
  duration that closes on its own after the dwell, unless the pointer or focus is in it.

Tokens
  --component-drawer-duration       300ms                         → motion/duration/slow
  --component-menu-duration         150ms                         → motion/duration/fast
  --component-toast-dwell           5000ms                        → motion/duration/dwell
  --motion-ease-entrance            cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)    → ease/decelerate
  --motion-ease-exit                cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)    → ease/accelerate

CSS

    transition: transform var(--component-drawer-duration) var(--motion-ease-entrance);

Tabular figures are the whole layout fix. Proportional digits change width every second, so the tile and everything beside it shuffle sixty times a minute. font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums holds every digit to one width and costs nothing.
Prompt for a coding agent 
Countdown

Build
  Count down to an end time from the server, not a duration counted on the client.
  Recompute from the clock on every tick with a one second timer that corrects its own
  drift, so a backgrounded tab comes back right rather than slow.

  Swap only the digits that changed, with a fade on the micro duration. At zero, replace
  the timer with the ended state in the same footprint, so nothing below it moves.

Tokens
  --motion-duration-micro           75ms                          → duration/75
  --motion-ease-standard            cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)    → ease/standard
  --component-countdown-digit       #242628                       → text/default

CSS
  .countdown-digit {
    color: var(--component-countdown-digit);
    font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
    transition: opacity var(--motion-duration-micro) var(--motion-ease-standard);
  }

Announcement
  The visible timer is aria-hidden. Beside it a visually hidden sentence states the end,
  "Sale ends Friday at 6 PM", and a polite live region updates only at meaningful
  points: each hour, then each minute in the last hour, then "Sale ended". Announcing
  every second makes the page unusable with a screen reader.

Keyboard
  Not focusable, because there is nothing to act on. A button beside it keeps its own
  place in the focus order.

Reduced motion
  Digits change in place with no fade. The countdown keeps running: it is information,
  not decoration.

Mobile
  The same tick. Units shorten, Days to D, only where a tile would otherwise wrap.

    The text field is the component. Both patterns fail the same way: the clever part works and typing does not. Keep the field typable, validate what is typed, and treat the list and the calendar as faster routes to the same value.
    Prompt for a coding agent 
    Combobox and date picker

Build
  Combobox follows the ARIA combobox pattern. The input keeps focus the whole time,
  aria-activedescendant points at the highlighted option, and the list opens on typing
  or Down. Filter as the person types, with no delay, and mark the matching characters
  with combobox/match. With nothing matching, keep the list open on the No match row so
  the field does not look broken.

  Date Picker keeps a typable field. The calendar is a faster way to fill it, never the
  only way. Today carries a ring; the selected day takes the selected background.

Tokens
  --component-menu-duration         150ms                         → motion/duration/fast
  --motion-ease-entrance            cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)    → ease/decelerate
  --motion-ease-exit                cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)    → ease/accelerate
  --component-select-option-hover   #FAFAFA                       → surface/sunken
  --component-combobox-match        #4D596A                       → action/primary
  --component-datepicker-day-selected-background #4D596A                       → action/primary

CSS
  .combobox-list,
  .datepicker-panel {
    transition-property: opacity, transform;
    transition-duration: var(--component-menu-duration);
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-entrance);
  }
  .combobox-list[data-state=closed],
  .datepicker-panel[data-state=closed] {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateY(-4px);
    transition-timing-function: var(--motion-ease-exit);
  }
  .combobox-option[data-active] { background: var(--component-select-option-hover); }

Keyboard
  Combobox: Down and Up move the active option, Enter selects and closes, Escape closes
  and keeps the typed text, a second Escape clears it. Announce the count, "4 results".
  Date Picker: arrows move by day, Page Up and Page Down by month, Home and End to the
  week edges, Enter selects. Focus returns to the field on close.

Reduced motion
  The list and the panel appear and disappear in place.

Mobile
  The list runs full width under the field. For a single date prefer input type="date":
  the native picker is the one people already know. Use the kit picker for ranges.

    Sheet in Figma

    Worked examples

    Three carried from a past client storefront. Each one is a principle you can reuse, not a one off fix.

    Scroll indicator that tracks but is not a control

    A gallery indicator that reflects scroll position and is not tappable. It reads as navigation, so people click it, nothing happens, and it feels broken.

    Rule Make read only indicators visually distinct from controls: no affordance, no hover state, no cursor change. If it should be tappable, spec it as a control with a focus state and a hit target of at least 44px.

    Auto advancing message

    A rotating announcement that crossfades between messages on a timer.

    Rule Advance every 5s, crossfade 300ms. Pause on hover and on focus within, because hover alone strands keyboard users. Hold the first message with prefers-reduced-motion, no auto advance. Never put the only path to an action inside a rotating message.

    Hover on desktop, shown by default on mobile

    A quickview or overlay revealed on hover at desktop width.

    Rule Touch has no hover, so there is nothing to wait for. Show the content by default on mobile rather than binding it to tap. A tap that reveals instead of navigating costs the person their expected action. This holds for every hover revealed pattern, quickviews included.

    Interactions page in Figma  ·  Worked examples sheet

    PreviousImage systemNext Components
    DocsBuilding blocksModules

    Modules

    Sections, grouped by what they are for

    87 module sets with 927 variants, on four pages. Global Modules holds the chrome every project needs. Landing, Ecommerce and Dashboard are optional pages a project can delete in one action, because no module on them owns a token. Sections are grouped by content purpose rather than by component type, because that is how a stakeholder looks for their page.

    DesignerEngineerBoth readingVariant axes, toggles and text as they appear in Figma.Adds an On Shopify row to all 87 modules: theme file, settings and blocks.The Figma properties and the On Shopify row together.

    The convention

    • Every module has a paired Desktop frame and Mobile frame of the same content.
    • Beside each, a Measurements frame stating the pixel dimensions and, where there is an image, the ratio.
    • The ratio comes from the Image System page. A proportion that is not one of the seven is a conversation, not a new frame.
    • Name the module for what it shows, not where it sits. Full Bleed Feature, not Homepage Section 2.
    No module defines a token. No module defines a tier 3 token of its own. Each borrows tier 2 roles and the tier 3 rows the components inside it already own, so a project can replace a module wholesale without leaving a variable pointing at a component that no longer exists. The retail modules on the Ecommerce page follow the same rule, and it is the reason that page is safe to delete.

    Responsive, and what that means here

    Every module now carries a Breakpoint axis with three values. Each variant pins itself to the matching mode in 04 Responsive, so an instance resolves that breakpoint's type scale wherever it is placed, and each carries a maximum width for its band. Desktop is 1024 up, Tablet 640 to 1023, Mobile below 640.

    The layout half

    A module reflows by wrapping, and a child that fills its row will not wrap unless it carries a minimum width. Every module sets a floor on the children that share a row, so the row breaks instead of crushing them. 390 minus the 16 pixel Mobile margin (grid/margin) each side leaves a 358 content box. Floors were set when that box was 310, so none sits above 310 and every one fits with room to spare.

    The type half

    Every heading style binds its size to the scale in 04 Responsive: Heading/H2 is 72 at Desktop, 48 at Tablet and 36 at Mobile. A frame that is not pinned to a mode renders desktop type at whatever width it happens to be, so a 390 frame shows a 72 pixel heading and the module looks broken when the layout is correct. Pin the frame first, then judge the layout.

    What the Tablet band fixed

    Tablet had never been rendered anywhere in the file, although 04 Responsive has carried Tablet values for all 17 tokens since it was built. Drawing it at 768 exposed three modules that read badly there, all from the old 1024 split treating 768 as a phone. Page Footer now runs two link columns instead of one. Media and Copy keeps its fifty fifty split, each half 368 pixels. Feature Row caps its card width so a wrapped third card stays card sized instead of stretching across the row with an image to match.

    What the band floor fixed

    A variant is authored at its band ceiling, so 1023 for Tablet and 639 for Mobile, and a layout that fits there can still fail at the bottom of the same band. The doc sheets render each variant at a real device width instead, 1440, 768 and 390, and that is the only place in the file a module is seen at a width a phone actually has. Checking it turned up nav links that need 835 pixels in a 768 bar, numbered pagination 18 wide of a 310 content box, and paired inputs whose two 240 floors cannot share a 244 column. Nav links now collapse to a menu button at Tablet, pagination drops to previous and next at Mobile, and any row holding two floors wraps, which costs nothing at widths where the pair still fits.

    A breakpoint axis is for content that differs, not width that differs. Every module carries one now. It started as a rule about content that differs rather than width that differs, and Site Header, Breadcrumb Bar and Media and Copy qualified on that test alone. The Tablet work extended it to all of them for the second reason: a variant pins its own mode in 04 Responsive, so the type scale resolves at the band rather than rendering desktop type at phone width.

    Every module uses the same three ranges: Desktop 1024 up, Tablet 640 to 1023, Mobile below 640.

    A theme block shared by the sale sections and the announcement bar. end_at reads the same dynamic source as Sale Countdown. Ended is a real state, so the block never sits at zero.

    A deadline as it will count down, in whole units. Inline sits in a section header; Tiles sits under a heading; Large is the content of the section. Seconds are off by default and turning them on is a decision: a value that changes every second is auto-updating content, so it needs a pause control and must not be announced to screen readers. Under reduced motion the digits change in place with no roll or flip. At zero, the section swaps to State=Ended and its action changes or goes; a timer frozen at 00 reads as broken.

    Build notes from the first modules

    Measurements, breakpoints and the reasoning recorded when the first modules were built. Variant counts are current; many of these sets have since gained layouts, which the cards above show.

    Site Header Modules · Page Chrome

    The site wide message strip above the navigation bar. A page holds one instance rather than two, so the pairing is decided once and not re-argued per template.

    24 variants on Layout x Breakpoint x State  ·  composes Utility Bar, Nav
    BreakpointMeasurementsBorrowed tokens
    Desktop1440 x 112None of its own.
    Tablet768 x 104
    Mobile390 x 96
    Range Desktop 1024 up, Tablet 640 to 1023, Mobile below 640.  ·  Floors none
    Reflow Fixed rows. Neither variant wraps.
    Why it is built this way. Desktop and Mobile are separate variants because Nav is. The band would reflow happily; a row of links and a hamburger are different content, not the same content at a different width.

    Site Header sheet in Figma

    Page Footer Modules · Page Chrome

    A brand column, three link columns and a legal row. This is the region both retail templates marked as a slot, so it is the one piece of chrome a project was previously expected to draw for itself.

    12 variants on Layout x Breakpoint  ·  composes Logo Slot, Divider
    BreakpointMeasurementsBorrowed tokens
    Desktop1440 x 330surface/sunken, border/subtle, text/default, text/muted
    Tablet768 x 465
    Mobile390 x 788
    Range Desktop 1024 up, Tablet 640 to 1023, Mobile below 640.  ·  Floors brand 260, columns 150
    Reflow Four columns across at 1024 up, one stacked column at 390. The legal row wraps too.
    Why it is built this way. The link columns are text, not Link instances. Link is an inline prose link and carries an underline in its resting state, which turns a column of four into a wall of rules. Nav sets the same precedent for navigation text.

    Page Footer sheet in Figma

    Page Title Band Modules · Page Headers

    The band that names the page: a title, an optional sentence under it, and on the second variant the actions that belong to the whole page rather than to something on it.

    6 variants on Layout x Breakpoint  ·  composes Button
    BreakpointMeasurementsBorrowed tokens
    Desktop1440 x 183surface/page, text/default, text/muted
    Tablet768 x 197
    Mobile390 x 244
    Range Desktop 1024 up, Tablet 640 to 1023, Mobile below 640.  ·  Floors copy 280
    Reflow Actions beside the copy, dropping underneath at about 700 and below.
    Why it is built this way. Use Simple unless the page really has a page level action. A button that acts on one row in a table belongs in the row, and moving it up here is how a page ends up with two primary actions.

    Page Title Band sheet in Figma

    Breadcrumb Bar Modules · Wayfinding

    The full width band that carries a Breadcrumb at the page margin, with a hairline under it. The band is the module and the path inside it is the component.

    3 variants on Breakpoint  ·  composes Breadcrumb
    BreakpointMeasurementsBorrowed tokens
    Desktop1440 x 56surface/page, border/subtle
    Tablet768 x 56
    Mobile390 x 48
    Range Desktop 1024 up, Tablet 640 to 1023, Mobile below 640.  ·  Floors none
    Reflow One line at every width. Truncated is how it stays one line.
    Why it is built this way. The hairline is what separates chrome from content. Without it a breadcrumb reads as the first line of the page. And a breadcrumb is not navigation for a page with no parent: leave the band out rather than showing a path of one.

    Breadcrumb Bar sheet in Figma

    Hero Landing · Feature Modules

    The opening moment of a page. Centred for the copy-only version, Banner for the ultra-wide crop with the copy sitting above it.

    6 variants on Layout x Breakpoint  ·  composes Button
    BreakpointMeasurementsBorrowed tokens
    Desktop1440 x 1156surface/page, surface/muted, text/default, text/muted
    Tablet768 x 782
    Mobile390 x 998
    Range Desktop 1024 up, Tablet 640 to 1023, Mobile below 640.  ·  Floors heading max 960, copy max 660
    Reflow Actions side by side above 640 and stacked below it. The media changes ratio rather than scale, 21:9 above 640 and 4:5 below, and the frame has its aspect ratio locked so a narrower instance keeps the crop.
    Why it is built this way. Copy over the photograph was built first and measured out of the question. The default treatment on the Text over image sheet is transparent for the top 45 percent, which leaves 339 of a 617 pixel ultra-wide frame, and the copy block is 539. The heading would have sat in the transparent part at 1.12 to 1. Copy above the image keeps contrast a known quantity and keeps the crop on an approved ratio. Anyone who does want type on the photograph is limited to what fits the bottom 55 percent, which means Heading/H3 or smaller and no body copy.

    Hero sheet in Figma

    Feature Row Landing · Feature Modules

    Two or three feature cards across a band: an image at 3:2, a heading, a short paragraph and a link.

    54 variants on Layout x Breakpoint  ·  image ratio 3:2  ·  composes Link
    BreakpointMeasurementsBorrowed tokens
    Desktop1440 x 661surface/page, surface/muted, text/default, text/muted
    Tablet768 x 1021
    Mobile390 x 1423

    Why it is built this way. The image is a plain filled slot, not an Image / Aspect Ratio instance. That set is a labelled specimen carrying its own dimensions as text, so instancing it into a module puts a wrong number on the page the moment the module resizes.

    Templates

    Whole pages, not parts of one

    A component answers what one control looks like. A module answers what a section looks like. A template answers what a page is made of, which is the question a client asks first and the one a kit of parts alone cannot settle. Nine templates: six retail, one marketing and two that any project can use, each built at Desktop 1440, Tablet 768 and Mobile 390 from module instances only.

    DesignerEngineerBoth readingBands top to bottom, and how to use a template in Figma.Adds how each template lands as a theme file, and the engineer steps.The Figma bands and the theme file view together.

    How to use it designer

    1. Open the anatomy sheet for the page you are building and read the When column. Required, Optional and Conditional are decisions somebody already made once, with the reason next to them.
    2. Duplicate the template frame for your breakpoint. It is pinned to its mode in 04 Responsive, so the grid and the type scale come with it.
    3. Replace copy and images inside the instances. Do not detach, and do not restyle: every control inherits its states from the core set.
    4. Draw the conditional regions separately. Loading, no results and bulk actions replace another region, so they are their own frame rather than a layer stacked on the template.

    How to use it engineer

    1. Read the anatomy table as the region contract. The Module column names the component that owns each region, so a region maps to one component rather than to a bag of markup.
    2. Treat the Slot regions as project work. Nothing in the token layer points at them: charts and bulk actions on the general pages. The retail footers and reviews are now Page Footer and Review Block.
    3. Take the gutter and the column count from 04 Responsive rather than from the template. The template is one instance of the grid, not the source of it.
    4. The two paired regions render twice. Records are a table at Desktop and a list at Mobile, and a sticky buy bar exists at one breakpoint only. Same data, two components.

    A client page goes into the kit template first. When a client brings its own pages, its default page of a type replaces the kit template of that type in place. Its other versions sit straight after it as named variants, labelled TEMPLATE · PRODUCT PAGE · CLIENT VARIANT, and a page type the kit lacks joins the closest category as a CLIENT ADDITION. Client adaptation has the full rule.

    What the three When values mean

    WhenWhat it obliges
    RequiredDraw it. A page missing a required region is missing something a shopper uses, not something a designer trimmed.
    OptionalA category decision. Skip it deliberately, and skip it on both pages rather than on one.
    ConditionalIt appears instead of another region, in a state the page can reach. Loading and no results replace the product grid; the sticky buy bar exists on Mobile only.

    PLP Listing page · Retail

    Ten regions. Seven are required, one is optional and two are conditional: they replace the grid rather than stacking above it.

    10 regions  ·  7 required · 1 optional · 2 conditional  ·  7 component sets: Utility Bar, Nav, Breadcrumb, PLP Header, Filter Panel, Product Tile, Pagination
    RegionModuleWhenThe rule
    01Utility bar Announcement Bar Optional One site wide message. Static for one, Rotating for two. Three is a carousel nobody reads.
    02Global nav Nav Required Desktop or Mobile per the breakpoint, never both drawn. Bind a layer to the two visibility flags in 04 Responsive rather than hiding it by hand.
    03Breadcrumb Breadcrumb Required The category path, so a shopper who arrived from search knows where they are. Truncated below 640.
    04Listing header PLP Header Required Category name, result count, sort and filter. The count is the part shoppers actually read, so it is not optional chrome.
    05Refinement Filter Panel Required Beside the grid on Desktop. On Mobile it is the same panel inside a Drawer, opened from the header, not a second design.
    06Product grid Product Tile Required Four across Desktop, two across Mobile, on the 04 Responsive grid. Never a fixed pixel gap: the gutter is a token.
    07Loading Skeleton Module Conditional The Product tile module, in the same grid at the same tile size, while the first page loads. It replaces the grid rather than sitting above it.
    08No results Empty State Conditional The No results reason, with its clear filters action. Never an empty grid and never a bare line of text.
    09Pagination Pagination Required Numbered on Desktop, Prev and next on Mobile. Infinite scroll is a project decision, not a kit default, and it needs a footer answer.
    10Footer Page Footer Required Page Footer, the Columns layout with social in the built template. The one region a client almost always has already, so expect its content rather than its layout to change.
    Notes.
    • Both template frames are pinned to their breakpoint mode in 04 Responsive, so the grid, the canvas and the type scale resolve without anyone switching a mode by hand. Duplicate the frame rather than rebuilding it.
    • Everything inside is an instance. Replace copy and images and leave the styling to the library, so a retone reaches the page without anyone reopening it.
    • Refinement sits beside the grid on Desktop only. On Mobile it is the same Filter Panel inside a Drawer, opened from the header, not a second design.

    PLP anatomy sheet  ·  PLP template, three breakpoints

    PDP Detail page · Retail

    Fourteen regions. Seven are required, five are optional and two are conditional. More of this page is negotiable than the listing page, because how much a shopper needs before deciding is a category question.

    14 regions  ·  7 required · 5 optional · 2 conditional  ·  13 component sets: Utility Bar, Nav, Breadcrumb, Image / Aspect Ratio, Carousel Indicator, Radio Group, Tag, Stepper, Button, Icon Button, Alert, Accordion, Product Tile
    RegionModuleWhenThe rule
    01Utility bar Utility Bar Optional As the listing page. If it is on one it is on both.
    02Global nav Nav Required As the listing page.
    03Breadcrumb Breadcrumb Required The path back to the listing, which is where most shoppers came from. Truncated on Mobile.
    04Gallery Image / Aspect Ratio Required One ratio per project, 1:1 or 4:5. Carousel Indicator underneath: Dots up to about six images, Bars past that.
    05Title and price Composed Required Product name and price. Take the sale and sold out treatment from Product Tile so the grid and the detail page cannot disagree.
    06Variant picker Radio Group, Tag Conditional Size as a Radio Group, because one option is always chosen. Colour as Tags with Selected on the current one. Only when the product has variants.
    07Quantity Stepper Optional Skip it where a shopper almost never buys two. At minimum is the state that stops it reaching zero.
    08Add to bag Button, Icon Button Required One primary action. Wishlist sits beside it as an Icon Button, never as a second Button competing for the same decision.
    09Delivery note Alert Optional The Info tone, one line, on shipping or returns. It is reassurance at the point of doubt, not somewhere to put policy.
    10Details Accordion Required Description, materials, care, shipping. First one open, the rest collapsed, so the page has a floor.
    11Reviews Review Block Optional Review Block Summary in the built template. On Shopify it is often a third party app block arriving with its own styling, which is worth budgeting for early.
    12Cross sell Product Tile Optional A row of four on Desktop, a horizontal scroll on Mobile. A row, not a second grid: the shopper is here to decide, not to browse again.
    13Sticky buy bar Composed Conditional Mobile only. Price and the primary action, appearing once the buy block has scrolled away. Do not draw a fake status bar above it.
    14Footer Page Footer Required Page Footer, as the listing page.
    Notes.
    • The buy column is composed rather than a component. Title, price and the sale treatment come from Product Tile, so the grid and the detail page cannot disagree about how a reduced price looks.
    • The sticky buy bar is Mobile only and appears once the buy block has scrolled away. It is drawn in place at the foot of the template frame rather than floating, so the height of the page reads honestly.
    • Reviews are Review Block and the footer is Page Footer in the built template. On a store with a reviews app, the reviews region becomes an app block carrying its own styling.

    PDP anatomy sheet  ·  PDP template, three breakpoints

    Dashboard Overview page · General

    Ten regions. Four are required, four are optional and two are conditional. The charts are the only regions the kit does not own, and that is deliberate.

    10 regions  ·  4 required · 4 optional · 2 conditional  ·  8 component sets: Site Header, Page Title Band, Stat Strip, Search, Select, Table, List Row, Page Footer
    RegionModuleWhenThe rule
    01Global nav Site Header Required The Site Header module. On an internal tool the strip above the navigation usually carries environment or account context rather than a promotion.
    02Page title Page Title Band Required The page name, and on the With actions variant the export or create action that belongs to the whole page rather than to a row in it.
    03Summary Stat Strip Required Three or four numbers, and the first thing anyone reads. If you cannot name the four, the dashboard does not have a purpose yet.
    04Filters Search, Select Optional A date range and one or two dimensions, in a single row above the charts. Never scattered between them, because a filter next to one chart reads as belonging only to that chart.
    05Primary chart Slot Required Not in the kit. The data visualisation sheet on Foundations sets the palette, the three series cap and the mark specs; the chart itself is project work in code.
    06Secondary charts Slot Optional Two smaller charts side by side, same palette and same cap. A third row of charts is usually two rows too many.
    07Recent activity Table, List Row Optional The last ten of something, with a link to the full list rather than pagination. A dashboard that paginates has quietly become a list page.
    08Loading Skeleton Module Conditional The Card and Table row modules in place, at the same count, so the layout does not jump when the numbers arrive.
    09Empty Empty State Conditional The empty account reason, for a workspace with no data yet. A dashboard of zeroes reads as broken rather than as new.
    10Footer Page Footer Optional Usually omitted on an internal tool. Keep it on anything a customer signs in to, because that is where the legal links live.
    Notes.
    • Both frames are pinned to their breakpoint mode in 04 Responsive, so a duplicate resolves its grid, canvas and type scale without anyone setting a mode.
    • The charts are dashed slots, not drawings. What the kit owns is the palette, the three series cap and the mark specs. A chart drawn in Figma would drift from the one in production inside a sprint.
    • Recent activity is a Table on Desktop and List Rows on Mobile. Same records, different component, because a six column table on a phone is a horizontal scroll nobody uses.

    Dashboard anatomy sheet  ·  Dashboard template, Desktop and Mobile

    List view Records page · General

    Ten regions. Five are required, two are optional and three are conditional. It is the closest non retail cousin of the listing page, and the differences are the interesting part.

    10 regions  ·  5 required · 2 optional · 3 conditional  ·  10 component sets: Site Header, Breadcrumb Bar, Page Title Band, Search, Select, Tag, Table, List Row, Pagination, Page Footer
    RegionModuleWhenThe rule
    01Global nav Site Header Required The Site Header module, as every other template.
    02Breadcrumb Breadcrumb Bar Optional Only where the list sits under something. A top level list has no path, and a path of one reads as a mistake.
    03Page title Page Title Band Required The With actions variant, because a list page almost always has a create action, and that action belongs to the page rather than to a row.
    04Filters and search Search, Select, Tag Required One row: search, one or two dimension filters, and the applied filters as Tags underneath. Not a sidebar. A list page is not a product grid, and a sidebar here costs a third of the table width.
    05Bulk actions Slot Conditional Appears in place of the filter row once a row is selected, carrying the selected count and the actions. Replacing the row rather than stacking above it is what stops the table jumping down the page.
    06The records Table, List Row Required Table on Desktop. On Mobile the same records as List Row, because a six column table on a phone is a horizontal scroll nobody uses. Same data, different component.
    07Pagination Pagination Required Numbered on Desktop, Prev and next on Mobile. A list page paginates: that is most of what separates it from a dashboard.
    08Loading Skeleton Module Conditional Table row on Desktop and List row on Mobile, at the count a full page holds, so the page does not resize under the reader.
    09No results Empty State Conditional Two different reasons live here: an empty list and a filter that matched nothing. They need different words and different actions, and using one for both is the most common empty state mistake.
    10Footer Page Footer Optional As the dashboard.
    Notes.
    • Filters sit in a row, not a sidebar. A refinement column costs a table three hundred pixels and forces a horizontal scroll, which is the one place where copying the listing page is the wrong instinct.
    • The applied filters are Tags in the Removable variant, under the controls. They are how a reader sees why a list is short before deciding the data is missing.
    • Bulk actions replace the filter row rather than stacking above it, which is what stops the table jumping down the page when a row is selected.

    List view anatomy sheet  ·  List view template, Desktop and Mobile

    A module never owns a token. Deleting the Ecommerce page orphans nothing. None of the retail modules define tier 3 tokens of their own, which is why they borrow progress/, card/, image/ and field/ rows rather than introducing product/ or plp/ groups. The one exception is countdown/, which Sale Countdown and its siblings need for a tile no core component draws.

    Patterns

    Component pairings

    Whole pages moved to the Templates page, which now holds four of them. What belongs here is the pairing that is neither one component nor one page: a Filter Panel inside a Drawer, a Quickview over a grid, a Toast landing while a Modal is open. Assemble from instances, and never rebuild a component or a module inline on this page.

    DesignerEngineerBoth readingThis page reads the same in every reading.

    Build order

    1. 1
      Foundations In the kit

      Tokens first, before a single component is touched.

    2. 2
      Components In the kit

      The thirteen-item floor. Bound to Tier 3, no hardcoded values.

    3. 3
      Modules In the kit

      Nine page level sections composed from components, on the Modules page. A project adds its own beside them.

    4. 4
      Templates In the kit

      Four whole pages composed from modules, on the Templates page. Anything past those four is project work.

    Migration order

    Global elements go first: the Site Header and Page Footer modules. Every template depends on that chrome, so a template built before it is a template that gets rebuilt. Listing and detail pages follow in Wave 2, and the kit already carries an anatomy and a built frame for each. Content and storytelling templates usually need marketing or brand sign-off, so start that conversation while the earlier waves are still in build rather than after.

    Pairings

    The Pairings sheet is where a pairing gets assembled from instances. It is empty in the file today, so there is nothing to show here yet. When a pairing is added, it goes beside the kit pattern or interaction it extends, with a Header, its states side by side, a Spec and Notes.

    PreviousTemplatesNext Shopify
    DocsPlatformShopify

    Platform

    How the kit lands on Shopify

    Most client work runs on Shopify, so the kit states how it lands there. This page is the contract between the Figma file and a theme: which kit concept becomes which Shopify concept, what a merchant can change, and where the platform limits bite. It assumes a headed build on Online Store 2.0, which is what a storefront project actually is. Polaris is Shopify admin, a different system for a different surface, and nothing here maps to it.

    DesignerEngineerBoth readingThe map, the contract and the notes. The theme code is on Engineer.Adds the theme code: settings schema, CSS layer and one section in full.Everything, including the theme code.
    What becomes whatSection contractTemplates to theme filesTheme handoffWhat stays with the project

    Why the kit maps cleanly onto this platform.

    Online Store 2.0 is a template made of sections, a section made of blocks, and settings scoped to whichever level owns the decision. The kit already separates components from modules from templates for its own reasons. Those two hierarchies line up almost exactly, which is why the mapping on the next sheet is a rename rather than a rebuild.

    The thing this is really for.

    A merchant building a landing page without a developer. That only works if the sections carry the right settings and the right presets, which is a design decision made here rather than a coding decision made later. The section contract on this page states every module’s settings and blocks, so the theme developer is implementing a spec rather than guessing one.

    Imagery is on its own page.

    Everything platform specific about images and video lives on the Image System page, on the Shopify platform sheet: the transform filter and its 5760 limit, the srcset widths per layout, the media types and where each one can live, and the six behaviours that cost people a day. It sits there rather than here so it stays next to the ratio family it depends on.

    What becomes what

    Read this left to right once and the rest of the page follows. The kit names things for what they are; Shopify names them for where they sit in the theme. Neither vocabulary is wrong, and a handoff goes badly when only one of them is written down.

    In the kitIn the themeWhat that means in practice
    Componentsnippet, or a theme blockA Button or a Badge is a snippet the theme renders. It becomes a theme block only when a merchant needs to place it themselves, which for most controls they never do.
    ModulesectionThe unit a merchant adds, removes and reorders. The kit ships 16 global, 31 landing and 34 ecommerce modules, and the section contract lists each one with its theme file, settings and blocks. Smaller parts such as Feature Item or Value Prop land as theme blocks, not sections.
    A module repeating childblockA Feature Item, a Metric, a Value Prop, an FAQ question. Theme blocks if the same child is wanted in more than one section, section blocks if it belongs to exactly one.
    Slot, or an app owned moduleapp block, or not theme workReviews are an app block, even though the kit now draws Review Block as the target to style the app toward. Checkout is Shopify hosted. The Dashboard modules are admin UI, not a storefront concern. Empty Section is the frame an app block sits in.
    TemplateJSON templatetemplates/index.json, collection.json, product.json, cart.json and 404.json, plus the alternate page templates page.landing.json, page.about.json and page.contact.json. The band order on each template sheet is the section order in the JSON.
    Site Header, Page Footersection groupsections/header-group.json and sections/footer-group.json. Groups exist so the chrome is editable without being part of every template.
    04 Responsive modesnothingThe theme does this with CSS. The modes exist so a designer can see the intent and so the type scale is one decision rather than nine. Do not look for them in Liquid.
    01 Primitives brand rampstheme settings, then CSS custom propertiesOne theme, one brand. The ramps become the colour scheme defaults and the brand preset; Theme handoff shows the split.

    The limits that shape a design

    A JSON template or section group renders at most 25 sections, and a section holds at most 50 blocks, or fewer when max_blocks says so; static blocks do not count toward either.

    More

    A section takes either theme blocks (@theme) or its own section blocks, never both, so the choice is made once per section. And a section or block without a preset in its schema cannot be added in the theme editor at all: it has to be written into the JSON by hand and cannot be removed. None of the ceilings are close on a project this size, but the preset rule and the one block model per section are correctness rules, and they are the ones that get missed.

    Where settings live is a design decision

    Shopify guidance is to group settings into blocks so the editor sidebar stays legible, and to avoid blocks so granular that a merchant has to assemble a paragraph out of four of them.

    More

    That is the same judgement as deciding what belongs in a component versus a module, so it belongs to whoever drew the module rather than to whoever writes the Liquid.

    Icons reach the theme as inline SVG snippets

    The theme takes icons exported from whichever library the 06 Icon Library mode has selected: Lucide or Tabler as strokes with stroke set to currentColor, Phosphor or Remix as fills with fill set to currentColor, so a colour scheme recolours them with no extra settings.

    More

    Names stay the Lucide names in every mode, so a snippet such as icon-search.liquid keeps its name when the library changes. The full recipe is on the Iconography page.

    Payment and social marks are the platform’s, not ours

    Payment icons render from shop.enabled_payment_types with payment_type_svg_tag, so the footer shows what the store actually accepts.

    More

    The Payment Method set on the Iconography page uses the same official marks from Shopify’s payment_icons, for design files only. Social icons are the Simple Icons marks, filled with currentColor in Mono and the brand colour in Brand, and their links come from the social settings in theme settings. Store badges stay placeholders until the official badge files are supplied.

    Architecture map in Figma

    The section contract

    One row per module, grouped as the module pages are: Global, Landing, Ecommerce, then Dashboard. The file a theme developer creates, the settings a merchant can change, and the blocks it accepts, named in Shopify schema types so a row can be typed up directly. A row whose file is a block or a snippet is a part, not something a merchant adds on its own. Every section row needs a preset, one per layout, or the merchant cannot add it in the editor.

    Dashboard modules 6

    Module and theme fileMerchant settings and blocksPreset and notes
    App Header, KPI Row, Chart Card, Chart Grid, Activity Panel, Dashboard Overviewnot theme workSettingsnoneBlocksnoneAdmin and internal tool UI. On Shopify that is an embedded app built with Polaris, a different system on a different surface. The modules stay in the kit for clients who also have an internal tool.

    A variant is not always a setting

    Three different things happen to the Figma variant axes. Count becomes the number of blocks the merchant adds.

    More

    Layout, Media and Align become a select, Tone and Ground become a colour scheme, and Show booleans become checkboxes one to one. Breakpoint becomes nothing, because CSS already does it. When a Layout axis grows past about eight options, as Hero Section and Feature Row have, it splits into one section per family rather than one long select.

    max_blocks is where a design rule becomes enforceable

    The kit says one action on a CTA Band, four numbers on a Stat Strip, four questions on an FAQ.

    More

    Written in a Notes block those are advice. Written as max_blocks they are the reason a merchant cannot break the design at 11pm before a launch. Every cap on this sheet traces back to a sentence on a module sheet.

    Colour scheme is the setting that carries the brand

    Every section takes color_scheme rather than individual colour pickers.

    More

    That is what connects a section to the brand layer: the schemes are generated from the semantic tokens, so a merchant picks a scheme and gets a combination the kit has already contrast checked. Individual colour pickers per section are how a themed system quietly stops being one.

    Section contract in Figma

    Templates to theme files

    The anatomy sheets on the Templates page list regions in the order a shopper meets them. That order is the order of sections in the JSON, so the two documents are the same document written for two audiences. Where a region is not a section, this says what it is instead, because that is the part a scope conversation turns on.

    Kit templateTheme fileOwnsHow the regions land
    Storefront Hometemplates/index.jsoneleven bandsAnnouncement, navbar and footer come from the section groups. Every band between them is its own section: hero, collection list, two featured collections, sale banner, value props, testimonials and featured blog. index.json is the template merchants reorder most, so every one of these needs a preset.
    PLPtemplates/collection.jsonregions 01 to 11Chrome comes from the header and footer groups. Breadcrumb Bar is drawn as its own band but lands as a theme block at the top of the first section. Product List Filter is two sections that always travel together: the title is main-collection-banner, and the toolbar, refinement, grid, loading, no results and pagination sit inside main-collection-product-grid, which is why regions 05 to 09 cannot be reordered against each other. Value Props is a section the merchant can move or drop.
    PDPtemplates/product.jsonregions 01 to 15Product Header is main-product. The breadcrumb, the gallery and every part of the Buy Box are theme blocks inside it: title and price, variant picker, quantity, buy buttons, delivery note and each collapsible tab. That is why the buy column can be reordered by a merchant without a developer. Value Props is a section, reviews are an app block, and cross sell is related-products reading the Product Recommendations API. The sticky buy bar is a mobile only block.
    Carttemplates/cart.jsonsix bandsCart Page is main-cart-items and main-cart-footer side by side. Value Props is a section and the product row is related-products driven by the cart contents. Cart Drawer and Mini Cart are not on this template: they are values of the cart_type theme setting, and the page still exists for links from emails.
    Landing pagetemplates/page.landing.jsontwelve bandsBuilt on the Templates page as Landing Page. An alternate page template plus presets on every landing module is what lets marketing build a campaign page without a developer. Add one alternate template per campaign shape rather than one per campaign; page.landing.json is the first.
    About and Contacttemplates/page.about.json
    page.contact.json    		seven bandsTwo alternate page templates sharing the same sections. Header Band opens both, and the contact form is the theme contact form, so submissions reach the admin with no app.
    404templates/404.jsonthree bandsmain-404 holds the heading, body and recovery links as settings and blocks. The header and footer groups still render, so the visitor has a way out.
    List viewtemplates/customers/orders.jsonregions 01 to 10The closest storefront home for it is the customer order history page, which is genuinely a records page with filters and pagination. Outside that, a list view on a Shopify project is usually an internal tool rather than a storefront page, and it is not theme work.
    Dashboardnot a themenothingNo storefront equivalent. The template now uses the Dashboard modules: App Header, KPI Row and Chart Card. On Shopify an operational dashboard is an embedded admin app built with Polaris, a different design system on a different surface. It stays in the kit because most clients have an internal tool somewhere.

    A region is not always a section, and that is a scope fact

    On the PLP, six regions live inside Product List Filter, which is two sections.

    More

    On the PDP, eight live inside main-product. A client reading the anatomy sheets will count twenty six regions and hear twenty six units of work, and a developer reading the templates will count far fewer sections. Both are right. Saying which is which before the estimate is how that conversation stops being a surprise.

    Two regions are drawn here but owned elsewhere

    Reviews are an app block. The kit draws Review Block so there is a target to style the app toward, but it arrives with a third party stylesheet and a shape the theme does not control.

    More

    Loading is CSS and script around the Skeleton Module drawing. Both are worth naming in a scope document, because a client will otherwise assume the design covers them.

    The landing page template is the one that saves the most time

    A merchant who can build a campaign page from existing sections does not raise a ticket, which is the whole argument for presets and settings schemas being a design deliverable rather than an implementation detail.

    More

    On a brand running one or two launches a quarter, that template pays for the kit on its own.

    Template map in Figma

    Theme handoff

    What a theme developer needs before writing a line: which tokens become merchant settings and which stay in CSS, the CSS layer that carries them, one section written out in full as the pattern every other row follows, the templates and features a standard theme has to cover, and the quality floor. The section contract says what each module is; this sheet says how to type it up.

    Tokens to theme

    Only what a merchant should change becomes a setting. Everything else is CSS the theme owns, written once and read by every section. The split is the same as the token tiers: brand values move per store, system values never do.

    In the kitIn the themeWho changes it, and how
    02 Semantic coloursettings_schema.json
    color_scheme_group    		The merchant, per scheme. Schemes are generated from the semantic roles (page, muted, inverse, brand) and seeded into settings_data.json, so the defaults are contrast checked before anyone edits them. Sections take color_scheme and nothing else.
    01 Primitives brand rampsnot a settingBaked into the scheme defaults and the brand preset. A second brand is a second preset in settings_data.json on the same theme, never a second theme.
    type/family display, textfont_picker ×2
    type_heading_font, type_body_font    		The merchant, from the Shopify font library. A licensed client face is @font-face from assets instead, which is fine for a custom theme and not accepted on the Theme Store.
    04 Responsive type scalefixed CSS
    clamp() or media queries    		Nobody in the editor. scale/h1 is 96 / 72 / 48 across the three bands; write it once in base.css.
    radius sm, md, lgfixed CSS, or one selectFixed by default. If a brand needs it, one select corner_style (sharp, soft) swaps the whole set. Never a radius per section.
    02 Spacingfixed CSS custom propertiesNobody. Density is a build decision. The only spacing a merchant touches is padding_block on some sections, a range over the section padding steps.
    02 Motionfixed CSS, plus prefers-reduced-motionNobody. Reduced is a media query that sets every duration to 0ms, exactly as the Reduced mode does in Figma.
    03 ComponentCSS custom properties in component CSSNobody. Component variables alias the semantic ones, so a scheme change reaches every button and field without a component setting.
    06 Icon Librarysnippets/icon-*.liquidThe developer, once: export the chosen library as inline SVG snippets. Not a setting.

    Settings · config/settings_schema.json

    Two groups carry the brand. Labels are locale keys, so the editor reads in the merchant’s language.

    config/settings_schema.json (excerpt)

          { "type": "color", "id": "button",                 "label": "t:settings_schema.colors.button",          "default": "#4D596A" },
          { "type": "color", "id": "button_label",           "label": "t:settings_schema.colors.button_label",    "default": "#FFFFFF" },
          { "type": "color", "id": "secondary_button",       "label": "t:settings_schema.colors.secondary_button","default": "#FFFFFF" },
          { "type": "color", "id": "secondary_button_label", "label": "t:settings_schema.colors.secondary_label", "default": "#242628" },

        ],

          "text": "text",
          "primary_button": "button",

Seed config/settings_data.json with four schemes from 02 Semantic, Light:
  scheme-1  page     background surface/page #FFFFFF, text text/default #242628
  scheme-2  muted    background surface/muted #F2F2F3, text text/default #242628
  scheme-3  inverse  background surface/inverse #242628, text text/inverse #FFFFFF
  scheme-4  brand    background action/primary #4D596A, text text/on-action #FFFFFF
Re-measure every scheme the merchant edits; the kit only vouches for the seeded values.

    The CSS layer · snippets/css-variables.liquid

    Rendered once in layout/theme.liquid. Scheme values arrive from settings; everything below them is the token tier written as custom properties with the names from the Token Reference page.

    snippets/css-variables.liquid
    {%- style -%}
  {{ settings.type_heading_font | font_face: font_display: 'swap' }}
  {{ settings.type_body_font | font_face: font_display: 'swap' }}

  :root {
    --font-heading-family: {{ settings.type_heading_font.family }}, {{ settings.type_heading_font.fallback_families }};
    --font-body-family:    {{ settings.type_body_font.family }}, {{ settings.type_body_font.fallback_families }};

    --radius-sm: 4px;   --radius-md: 8px;   --radius-lg: 16px;   --radius-full: 9999px;
    --inset-sm: 8px;    --inset-md: 12px;   --inset-lg: 16px;    --inset-2xl: 24px;
    --stack-sm: 8px;    --stack-md: 12px;   --inline-sm: 8px;    --inline-md: 12px;
    --space-section-gap: 96px;              --space-section-padding-block: 80px; --space-section-padding-block-sm: 64px; --space-content-gap: 40px; --space-content-gap-lg: 64px; --grid-margin: 40px;                    --grid-gutter: 24px;

    --motion-duration-micro: 75ms;  --motion-duration-fast: 150ms;
    --motion-duration-base: 200ms;  --motion-duration-slow: 300ms;
    --motion-ease-standard: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);
    --motion-ease-entrance: cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1);
    --motion-ease-exit:     cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1);
  }

  @media (max-width: 1023px) { :root { --space-section-gap: 64px; --space-section-padding-block: 56px; --space-section-padding-block-sm: 48px; --space-content-gap: 32px; --space-content-gap-lg: 48px; --grid-margin: 24px; --grid-gutter: 16px; } }
  @media (max-width: 639px)  { :root { --space-section-gap: 48px; --space-section-padding-block: 40px; --space-section-padding-block-sm: 40px; --space-content-gap: 24px; --space-content-gap-lg: 32px; --grid-margin: 16px; } }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    :root { --motion-duration-micro: 0ms; --motion-duration-fast: 0ms; --motion-duration-base: 0ms; --motion-duration-slow: 0ms; }
  }

  {% for scheme in settings.color_schemes -%}
    .color-{{ scheme.id }} {
      --surface-page:   {{ scheme.settings.background }};
      --text-default:   {{ scheme.settings.text }};
      --text-muted:     {{ scheme.settings.text_muted }};
      --text-link:      {{ scheme.settings.link }};
      --action-primary: {{ scheme.settings.button }};
      --text-on-action: {{ scheme.settings.button_label }};
      --border-default: {{ scheme.settings.border }};
      background: var(--surface-page);
      color: var(--text-default);
    }
  {% endfor %}
{%- endstyle -%}

Every section wrapper adds class="color-{{ section.settings.color_scheme }}", and component CSS
reads only these variables, so --component-button-primary-background is var(--action-primary).

    One section in full · sections/cta.liquid

    The CTA Section row from the contract, written out. Every other row follows the same shape: settings in contract order, one block model, max_blocks from the design rule, labels as locale keys, and one preset per layout.

    sections/cta.liquid · schema
    {% schema %}
{
  "name": "t:sections.cta.name",
  "tag": "section",
  "class": "section-cta",
  "disabled_on": { "groups": ["header", "footer"] },
  "settings": [
    {
      "type": "select", "id": "layout", "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.layout.label",
      "options": [
        { "value": "centered",   "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.layout.options.centered" },
        { "value": "split",      "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.layout.options.split" },
        { "value": "media",      "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.layout.options.media" },
        { "value": "media_card", "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.layout.options.media_card" },
        { "value": "signup",     "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.layout.options.signup" }
      ],
      "default": "centered"
    },
    {
      "type": "select", "id": "width", "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.width.label",
      "options": [
        { "value": "narrow", "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.width.options.narrow" },
        { "value": "full",   "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.width.options.full" }
      ],
      "default": "full"
    },
    { "type": "checkbox", "id": "show_secondary_link", "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.show_secondary_link.label", "default": false },
    { "type": "image_picker", "id": "image", "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.image.label" },
    { "type": "color_scheme", "id": "color_scheme", "label": "t:sections.cta.settings.color_scheme.label", "default": "scheme-4" }
  ],
  "blocks": [{ "type": "@theme" }, { "type": "@app" }],
  "max_blocks": 2,
  "presets": [
    {
      "name": "t:sections.cta.presets.centered",
      "settings": { "layout": "centered" },
      "blocks": [{ "type": "button", "settings": { "label": "Shop the range" } }]
    },
    {
      "name": "t:sections.cta.presets.signup",
      "settings": { "layout": "signup", "color_scheme": "scheme-2" },
      "blocks": [{ "type": "email-signup" }]
    }
  ]
}
{% endschema %}

    The theme code (settings_schema.json, the CSS layer and one section written out in full) is on the Engineer and Both readings.

    Templates and features a standard theme covers

    The Theme Store requirements are the checklist developers already use, even on a custom theme that will never be listed. Where the kit draws it, the module is named. Where it does not, it is theme code or a gap to scope.

    RequirementIn the kitWhat to do
    index, collection, product, cart, 404, page.contact, password, gift_cardtemplates drawnCovered by the Templates page and the contract. gift_card stays Liquid.
    search.json with filtersSearch Overlay, Product List FilterThe search results page reuses main-collection-product-grid with filtering, so search and collection filter the same way.
    blog.json, article.jsonBlog Section, Rich Text SectionCovered by the contract rows. Not drawn as page templates; the modules are the template.
    page.json, list-collections.jsonHeader Band, Rich Text, Category GridNo template drawn. page.json is Header Band plus Rich Text; list-collections is Category Grid reading every collection.
    Custom Liquid section and blockgapTheme code only: sections/custom-liquid.liquid and blocks/custom-liquid.liquid, available wherever app blocks are.
    App blocks in main-product and featured productProduct Header, Sale SpotlightBoth take @app. Keep it on any section a review, subscription or upsell app might target.
    Complementary products, pickup availabilitygapTwo buy column theme blocks to add: complementary products (Product Recommendations API, intent complementary) and pickup availability.
    Selling plans, Shop Pay Installments, unit pricingPrice covers unit pricingAdd a purchase options block to the buy column and render payment_terms in the price block. Unit price already has price/unit.
    Gift card recipient formgapA buy column block shown only for gift card products.
    Accelerated checkout, discounts, multi-level menus, newsletter, localizationBuy Box, Cart Summary, Mega Menu, email signup, Locale SelectorCovered.
    Rich media, variant images, image focal pointsProduct Header, Image SystemThe gallery renders image, video, external video and 3D model media, and every image honours its focal point through object-position.
    Follow on Shop, account componentgapHeader and footer entry points, with the login_button filter for Follow on Shop. Confirm classic or new customer accounts first.
    The quality floor, before a build is called done. Lighthouse performance of at least 60 and accessibility of at least 90, averaged across the home, product and collection pages on desktop and mobile. That is the Theme Store minimum and it is the right floor for client themes too. Native CSS with no Sass, unminified source, script as custom elements loaded with defer, images through image_url and image_tag at the srcset widths on the Image System page with width and height set so nothing shifts, and every animation reading the motion variables so the reduced motion query reaches it. Contrast is already measured in the kit; re-measure only the schemes a merchant edits.

    Theme handoff sheet in Figma

    What does not live here

    This page holds platform knowledge, which is why it ships with the kit rather than with a client. The list below is the part that is different on every project and belongs in the project file, and keeping the boundary honest is what stops this page going stale the first time a client does something unusual.

    • Which sections a given store actually uses, and in what order on each template. The kit says what a section is for; the project says where it goes.
    • The brand values themselves. The ramps here are demonstration values, stepped to prove the mechanism and contrast checked, not a recommendation for anybody.
    • Metafield and metaobject definitions. A bundle builder, a routine, a size guide and an ingredient list are all metaobjects, and their shape is a content model decision made with the client rather than a platform default.
    • Which apps are in play, and therefore which regions are app blocks. Reviews, subscriptions, loyalty and search all arrive with their own markup, and the design has to survive it rather than assume it away.
    • Anything about a specific store split, catalogue cleanup or migration. Those are project mechanics and they change monthly.
    The one rule that keeps this page useful. If a sentence here could only be true for one client, it is in the wrong file. The Image System page already works this way with its platform sheets, and it is the reason that page survived a client change without an edit.
