    Code registry

    Optional, for previews and handoff. Designers work in Figma and never need this page: it is for whoever builds the client site, or a designer who wants a clickable prototype. The kit in React and Tailwind, published as a shadcn registry. One command adds the tokens, then any component or module drops into a project with its kit name. Claude, Cursor or VS Code can browse and install it through the shadcn MCP.

    DesignerEngineerBoth readingThis page reads the same in every reading.

    Set up a project

    Works in any project that already uses shadcn with Tailwind 4 (Next.js, Vite, Astro, React Router). Add the registry to components.json, then install the tokens. The tokens step writes styles/lazer-tokens.css and adds its import to your global CSS.

    components.json
    "registries": {
  "@lazer": "https://lazer-ds-kit-site.vercel.app/r/{name}.json"
}
    Terminal
    npx shadcn@latest add @lazer/lazer-tokens
npx shadcn@latest add @lazer/hero-section @lazer/feature-row

    Load Inter and IBM Plex Mono in the app, or the retoned client faces; the tokens name the family and fall back to the system font. Dark is .dark or data-theme="dark", Compact density is data-density="compact", and reduced motion follows the OS or data-motion="reduced". Breakpoints match the kit: Desktop 1024 and up, Tablet 640 to 1023, Mobile below 640.

    What is in it

    ItemTypeWhat it is
    @lazer/lazer-tokensstyleAll 543 shipping tokens as CSS custom properties, every mode, one class per text style, and the shadcn theme variables mapped onto the kit. Install it first.

    Every class reads a kit token through var(--...) with the same name as the Figma code syntax, so a retone in 01 Primitives flows into code by regenerating one file. This is a pilot: eight items checked against Figma at 1440 and 390 and in Dark. The other components and modules follow the same pattern.

    Use it from Claude or Cursor

    The shadcn MCP server lets an assistant search, view and install items from any registry in components.json, including @lazer. Set it up once in the project, then ask in plain words, such as add the Lazer hero section to the home page.

# or --client cursor, --client vscode

    Iconography

    Iconography

    146 glyphs in one Icon set, drawn in four libraries: Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor and Remix. The 06 Icon Library mode picks which one renders, per page, per frame or for the whole file. They are grouped into eleven usage tiers so the working set is obvious and the long tail stays out of the way. Every glyph on this page redraws when you switch library, here or on the bar above the set.

    DesignerEngineerBoth readingHow a designer picks an icon in Figma.How an engineer imports an icon.Both, side by side.

    Four libraries, one set

    The kit draws every one of its 146 icons in four open source libraries. A variable collection, 06 Icon Library, decides which drawing shows, so a client gets its library with one mode change and no component is swapped, renamed or detached. Try it on this page: the switch below redraws every glyph here the way Figma does.

    Library
    Lucide · ISC · stroke 2

    Switching in Figma

    One page

    Click an empty spot on the canvas so nothing is selected. In the right panel’s Page section use Apply variable mode, then 06 Icon Library, then the library. Auto goes back to the file default.

    One frame

    Select the frame and use Apply variable mode in the Layer section. A frame setting beats the page setting, which is how one mockup can show a different library from the rest.

    The whole file

    In the Variables panel, drag the chosen mode to the first column of 06 Icon Library. The first column is the default everywhere nothing overrides it. Lucide ships first.

    How it is built

    The collection

    06 Icon Library has four modes, Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor and Remix, and four BOOLEAN variables, library/lucide, library/tabler, library/phosphor and library/remix. Each is true only in its own mode.

    Inside every Icon variant

    The original Lucide vectors stay as direct children, their visibility bound to library/lucide. Three frames named Tabler, Phosphor and Remix sit at 0,0 with scale constraints, each visible only when its boolean is true. Names stay Lucide in every mode, so nothing downstream changes.

    Stroke or fill

    Lucide and Tabler are strokes: colour on the stroke, bound to icon/default, weight bound to the icon stroke tokens. Phosphor and Remix are fills, so a recolour is set on the fill. Figma edits only the drawing that is visible, so a recolour made later has to be repeated in each mode.

    The star

    Phosphor and Remix stars carry an extra Fill vector, empty by default, under the outline. Rating instances set its fill, so a filled star stays filled in every library.

    Contrast by library

    Colour ratios do not change between libraries; the drawn line does. Every visible Icon instance, 4,860 of them, was resolved to its colour and ground in both modes and rendered in each library at 16, 20, 24 and 32. All 90 colour pairs clear 3.0, and every primary role clears 3.0 rendered in all four libraries. Phosphor regular is the light one: a pair needs roughly 4.5 as a colour to stay above 3.0 once drawn at 16.

    icon/muted at 16 onLucideTablerPhosphorRemix
    White4.225.254.105.07
    Warm #EFEAE33.654.413.564.28
    #F6F3F03.894.763.794.61
    Dark #2426285.286.205.166.05
    Dark #3A3D403.934.483.864.39

    rating/star-empty and tracker/upcoming-icon now alias icon/muted rather than text/disabled, because they carry meaning; they rendered below 3.0 in Lucide before the change. Disabled states keep text/disabled, which WCAG 1.4.11 exempts.

    Approximate drawings and licences

    Where a library has no exact match

    • package-check: Tabler package-import, Phosphor package, Remix checkbox-circle.
    • bookmark-check: Tabler plain bookmark.
    • search-x: Phosphor magnifying-glass-minus, Remix search-eye.
    • rotate-3d: Phosphor cube-focus, Remix box-3.

    Redraw these for a client that leans on them. Everything else is the library’s own glyph of the same meaning.

    Licences

    • Lucide ISC, lucide-static 1.43.0.
    • Tabler MIT, @tabler/icons 3.48 outline.
    • Phosphor MIT, @phosphor-icons/core 2.1.1 regular, fill for the star.
    • Remix Remix Icon License 1.0, remixicon 4.9.1 line. Allowed inside a design system as a minor part; not allowed sold as a pack, as a competing set, or as a logo. Not Apache 2.0, whatever older notes say.

    One library per product. A kit may ship a choice; a client file may not ship a mixture.

    Iconography · Switching icon library, in Figma

    The whole library is a single set with one Name property. Drop an Icon instance, then pick the glyph from the dropdown in the properties panel. There is no separate component per icon to hunt for, and nothing to detach.

    These are Lucide at their published names, so the names below are the import names. Nothing was redrawn and nothing was renamed, which means an upstream update is a version bump rather than a redraw. The glyphs on this page are the real Lucide paths, inlined at lucide-static 1.43.0.

    Size

    Three steps, each aliasing a spacing primitive. An icon does not carry a size of its own: it takes the one the component it sits in asks for.

    icon/size/sm16px · Inline in a table cell, a badge or a byline
    icon/size/md20px · The default, and what a button label expects
    icon/size/lg24px · Standalone, or a nav or empty state

    Colour

    Six roles, every one an alias of a text role, so an icon beside a label always matches that label rather than drifting from it. An icon inside a component inherits from that component's own rows, which is why a Button icon needs no setting.

    icon/defaulttext/default · #242628
    icon/mutedtext/muted · #666A70
    icon/interactiveaction/primary · #4D596A
    icon/disabledtext/disabled · #7E848B
    icon/inversetext/inverse · #FFFFFF
    icon/on-actiontext/on-action · #FFFFFF

    Stroke

    Two weights, and the second one is the exception rather than a choice.

    icon/stroke-lg2px at 24 · At 24, the weight the set is drawn at.
    icon/stroke-md1.67px at 20 · At 20, 2px scaled by the size.
    icon/stroke-sm1.33px at 16 · At 16, same again. Figma will not scale a stroke for you.

    The set

    The working set, not the library. 146 glyphs are imported, each drawn in all four libraries, out of roughly 1,800 in Lucide alone. Tier 01 Core is the set almost every screen touches. The rest come in through the official Lucide Figma Community plugin when a project actually needs one, so the file does not carry 1,700 components nobody uses.

    Changing the icon set

    One set ships, and a client that needs a different one swaps the whole set rather than part of it. Icon libraries disagree about more than drawing style: grid size, stroke weight, terminal shape, corner radius, and which metaphor stands for the same idea. Two sets on one screen reads as a mistake to people who could not say why, which is what makes mixing the most visible kind of drift a system has.

    Screen the licence before anything else. This file is copied into every engagement, so the icons are redistributed with it. That rules some sets out on paper rather than on taste.
    SetLicenceWhat it means for a kit
    LucideISCThe kit set. No attribution clause, which is why it was chosen for a file that gets copied.
    TablerMITRedistributes cleanly.
    PhosphorMITRedistributes cleanly. Ships six weights, so pick one before it enters the file.
    RemixRemix Icon License v1.0Attribution is appreciated rather than required, but redistributing the library means carrying the licence text and the copyright notices with it.
    HugeiconsMIT free tier, proprietary paid setThe free tier is fine. The paid set forbids redistributing its Figma source inside a template or a UI kit, which is exactly what this file is.
    ThenWhy
    Redraw, do not rewireEvery consumer reaches a glyph through the Name property on the single Icon set or through one of the ten swap slots, so a set change replaces the variants in place and touches none of the component sets that consume them.
    Keep the numbered prefixesThey remain the only control over dropdown order, and Core stays measured from real instance counts rather than guessed.
    Retune the stroke tokensicon/stroke-lg is 2 and icon/stroke-sm is 1.5 because Lucide draws at 2px on a 24 grid. A set drawn on a different grid resets both numbers, and the 16px rebinding rule has to be rechecked.
    Keep one weightA set with a weight axis gets one weight chosen and the rest left out. Six weights in the hands of a client team is a governance problem rather than a feature.
    Re-measure icon on background28 pairs at the 3.0 non-text floor, in both modes. A heavier line changes apparent contrast even where no token moved.

    One meaning per glyph, per project. A glyph can appear on more than one surface, and truck meaning shipping on a product page and delivery in a cart is the same idea in two places. What is not fine is one glyph carrying two ideas: star is a rating, so a saved item is a heart, not a star.

    How icons reach a theme

    The headline is an absence. Shopify publishes no storefront icon library, no icon setting type and no icon folder convention, so the set, the naming, the option keys and the accessibility treatment are all this kit's responsibility with no platform default to inherit.

    There is no icon setting type

    The settings schema documents thirty one input types and none of them is icon. Neither the section schema nor the theme block schema has an icon attribute either. So a merchant changeable icon is always a select over a list the theme owns, or an uploaded image. Whatever this kit calls a glyph is what ends up hard coded in the schema.

    Icons ship as inlined SVG, under 15 KB

    The one official helper is inline_asset_content, which takes an SVG from the theme assets folder and writes it into the page. The asset must be under 15 KB to inline, and Shopify's own documented example is literally icon.svg. Above that limit it silently does not inline.

    The CDN will not size an SVG

    An SVG cannot be resized or cropped by the image CDN unless a raster format is also requested, at which point it is a picture rather than a vector. Inline it and size it in CSS. With the 15 KB limit, this is what forces the set to stay small, simple and single stroke.

    One snippet has a 256 KB ceiling

    Liquid files other than JSON templates cap at 256 KB, so a single monolithic snippet holding the whole set will eventually hit it. Keep the glyphs as assets and inline them, or split the snippet. The file count, which caps at a hundred thousand, is never the problem.

    A long icon list belongs in a section

    settings_schema.json caps at 512 KB and a schema name caps at twenty five characters, so a long icon select lives in the section that needs it rather than in theme wide settings.

    Do not redraw payment marks or placeholders

    Shopify generates payment marks through payment_type_svg_tag, with an image role and a matching title element, and image placeholders through placeholder_svg_tag. Both are the platform's to render.

    The bag count is its own section

    The Cart API documents bundled section rendering, and its own example names a cart icon bubble section alongside a cart live region section, both re-fetched whenever the cart changes. The count on the bag has to re-render on its own.

    A social icon set is mandatory for the Theme Store

    A theme submitted to the Shopify Theme Store must offer a set of social media icons for a merchant to choose from. That is the one fixed icon list the platform actually requires.

    Three to one, and twenty four by twenty four

    An icon needs a contrast ratio of 3.0 against its background, and a pointer target must be at least twenty four by twenty four CSS pixels. Both are Theme Store requirements, so they gate whether a theme ships.

    Decorative icons carry an empty alt

    The documented rule is an empty alt attribute so a screen reader skips a decorative image. It is written for image elements and Shopify publishes nothing about inline SVG, which is how icons arrive. The nearest official signal is its own payment mark markup.

    What is not documented, and should not be treated as a contract. Dawn's icon snippets, its naming convention and the fixed icon list some of its sections offer are readable in its source but are not in Shopify's documentation. The same goes for aria conventions on icon only buttons, any screen reader text class, and the internals of the cart bubble section. Copy them if they help, but do not write them into a client's system as platform behaviour.

    Client adaptation

    Adapting the kit to a client

    This is the job the kit exists for. Duplicate the kit, paste one prompt, and it becomes the client’s system: tokens retoned, logo fitted, their old design system audited into the kit’s categories, and their photography in every image slot. The reference below is what the prompt does and why.

    DesignerEngineerBoth readingThis page reads the same in every reading.
    Duplicate first. Every adaptation runs in a copy of the kit. The master is never retoned, and the client’s old design system is read only throughout.

    Ten steps

    StepWhatWhat it means
    0Find everything in the sourcesColours, typefaces, weights, radius and the logo, read from the old system, brandbook and imagery. Asks only for what it could not find.
    1Build the rampsFull ramps that hit every rung the kit consumes, contrast checked before anything is bound.
    2Stop and show the rampsThe approval gate. Nothing is written until you say yes.
    3Write the valuesInto 01 Primitives only, in place. Never rename, never delete.
    4Walk it in DarkTwenty rungs are consumed only in Dark.
    5Chart palette, icon library, logoRe-derive the 23 chart steps, set 06 Icon Library, place the logo. 5B fits it to every component that uses it.
    6Re-measure, with numbersA measured ratio per line of the re-measure list, both modes.
    7Update the Token ReferenceThe reference sheets show the client values, not the kit’s.
    8Audit the client design systemEvery item is the same, similar or missing. Same maps, similar becomes a variant or a value, missing is built and placed by category.
    9Migrate the imageryOriginals into a Client imagery sheet, then every image instance filled.

    The same steps live on the Governance page in Figma as the Adaptation runbook sheet and the Brand adaptation prompt sheet. Adaptation runbook in Figma

    Adapting to a client brand

    The Read Me carries the thirteen step adaptation checklist, and that is the sequence to follow. This sheet is the colour depth behind three of its steps: what the ramps have to contain before you start, what actually consumes them, and what has to be re-measured once they move. Everything here is read out of the file, so the rung list is what something really binds to rather than what the ramps happen to hold.

    Where this sits in the checklist

    StepWhat it isWhat it requires
    Before 02Build the ramps firstA client hands over two or three hexes and a logo. The system consumes specific rungs, listed below, so the first task is turning those hexes into full ramps that hit every one of them. Skipping this is what makes a retone take a week: you get halfway through and find there is no step dark enough for text on a tint.
    Step 02Two consumption pathstype/family and type/style are consumed by the eleven text styles rather than by a variable alias, so they look unused in a token audit and are the opposite of unused. Load the client fonts in Figma before setting them, or the change fails silently.
    Step 03Retone tier 1, and only tier 1120 of the 147 primitive rows are load bearing. Change values in place. Never rename and never delete: a token name is the contract every tier above depends on.
    Step 03Re-derive the chart paletteRun the validator per mode, snap each slot to the nearest passing step of the client ramps, then work out the series cap again. It may not be three for a different set of hues. Never hand pick these.
    Step 06Walk it in Dark as well as LightTwenty primitive rungs are consumed only in Dark mode, so the step 06 walkthrough done in Light alone can be twenty rungs wrong and still look finished.
    Step 07Re-measure what sits on a moved groundThe contrast pass covers text. It does not cover a rule against its ground, or a badge edge against a selected row, because neither side is text. The re-measure list at the bottom of this sheet is what step 07 misses.

    What the client palette has to supply

    A rung not listed here is headroom. Leave it at whatever the ramp generator gives you.

    Two consumption paths, not one. Most primitives are reached by a variable alias, which any token audit will show you. Seven are reached by a text style instead: the three type/family rows and the four type/style rows. They look unused in an alias graph and they are the opposite of unused. Change a family and every heading in the library follows. Miss it and the client ships with Inter.

    The rungs that only Dark uses

    Nothing in Light points at these twenty, so a light mode review cannot catch them. Set the frame to Dark and walk the component sheets.

    color/brand/200color/brand/300color/brand/800color/accent/200color/accent/300color/neutral/700color/neutral/950color/neutral/400color/utility/error/200color/utility/error/800color/utility/success/800color/utility/warning/800color/utility/info/800color/alpha/black/40color/alpha/black/56color/chart/magenta/400color/chart/green/400color/chart/violet/300color/chart/red/200color/chart/red/400

    The re-measure list

    Colour is not a per token change. Move a ground and the things sitting on it have to be checked again. Most of these are invisible to an automated audit, because neither side is text.

    1. 01

      Text contrast. AA 4.5 for body, and 7.0 on the primary and destructive grounds because those two carry the most weight. 3.0 for anything non-text.

    2. 02

      Hairline perceptibility. A 1.2 ratio floor for a decorative rule, and 3.0 for a control boundary. Two different jobs: a divider separates content, while a field border is the only thing saying where the input is, because field/background matches surface/page. Measure border/strong and border/strongest at 3.0, and border/default and border/subtle at 1.2.

    3. 03

      Control boundaries after a retone. border/strong is the resting boundary for every input, select, stepper, pagination button, swatch, checkbox, radio and secondary button. border/strongest is the hover and selected state above it. A brand that lightens the neutral ramp can drop both below 3.0 without moving one text pair, so measure them against field/background and surface/page in both modes.

    4. 04

      Badge edges on a selected row. Every badge ground sits within three percent luminance of the selected row. badge/info/background against brand/100 measures 1.005. That is why every tinted tone carries a mid rung 1px edge, and a new brand hue can change which tones need one.

    5. 05

      The three rule tokens. table/border, listrow/border and row-hover collided at ratio 1.00 once already. When a state ground moves, re-measure the rules that sit on it.

    6. 06

      Destructive hover in Dark. action/destructive-hover needs a rung between the error ramp 100 and 500, or Dark loses its hover state entirely.

    7. 07

      The chart palette. Re-run the validator per mode, snap each slot to the nearest passing step, then re-derive the series cap.

    8. 08

      Dark on every sheet. Every component sheet carries a dark block. Look at all of them, because twenty primitive rungs are consumed only in Dark.

    9. 09

      Icons in the chosen library. Colour contrast is the same in every icon library; what reaches the eye is not. Phosphor regular is drawn at 1.5 and reads lighter, so a pair needs roughly 4.5 as a colour to stay above 3.0 once rendered at 16. Re-run the rendered check from Iconography, Contrast by library, in the library the client ships.

    What you never edit

    Tiers 2, 3 and 4. If a retone has you opening 02 Semantic, you are either adding a role the system genuinely lacks, which is fine and rare, or you are working around a ramp that is missing a rung, which is the actual problem.

    More

    05 Docs is not part of an adaptation either: it styles this documentation and never reaches a client surface.

    Open gap: leading is bound to nothing

    All four type/leading rows exist, but the eleven text styles set line height as a literal value rather than binding it.

    More

    So retoning leading has no effect today. That matters here specifically, because leading is exactly what changes when a client typeface does. Binding is not the fix: Figma reads a FLOAT bound to lineHeight as pixels, so 1.4 renders as 1.4px, and forcing the unit back to percent silently drops the binding. Tested on Heading/H1 and reverted. So the four rows stay documentation only, or they get dropped.

    The prompt that runs it

    A designer starting a client project does not have to remember any of the runbook. They paste the block below into Claude with the Figma MCP connected, fill six slots, and it runs the adaptation: it derives the ramps, stops for approval, writes into 01 Primitives only, walks the file in Dark, and reports a measured contrast ratio per line. When the client has an old design system, it then audits everything in it, components, modules, patterns and templates, maps each to its kit equivalent, and after a second approval updates the matches and builds the ones the kit lacks. The runbook is the reference behind it. This is the thing you actually run.

    How to use it

    1. 01

      The file URL. The client copy of the kit, not this one.

    2. 02

      The client sources. Their old Figma design system, their brandbook, or both. Claude reads every colour style, colour variable, text style, font and logo out of them, and every component, module, pattern and template; you do not type hexes.

    3. 03

      Fonts installed or not. If the licensed fonts are not on the machine running Figma, Claude stops before type and hands you the exact rows to set by hand.

    4. 04

      Check the manual add list. Anything Claude could not find or could not write is listed with where it goes and how to add it. Approve the ramps; Claude then fits the logo to every header and footer and brings Token Reference up to date, new colour groups and typefaces included. Last, if the client gave you its own design system, approve the client system map. Claude keeps what is the same, migrates what is similar into the matching kit item, adds what is missing, and reports a coverage count until every client component, module, pattern, template and page is accounted for.

    This is the thing you actually run. Paste it into Claude with the Figma MCP connected and fill the six client sources at the top. It reads the colours, type, radius and logo out of those sources itself, stops for your approval of the ramps, writes into 01 Primitives, walks the file in Dark, fits the logo, audits the client design system into the kit, migrates the photography, and reports a measured ratio per line of the re-measure list.

    What to have in hand

    1. A duplicate of the kit. Never the master. Paste the copy’s URL as the file.
    2. The old design system, as a Figma link, read only. Step 8 audits every component, module, pattern and template in it.
    3. The brandbook and imagery, as links or pages placed on Scratch. Colours, type, radius and the logo are found in them, so you type nothing they already say.
    4. Fonts installed, or not. If they are not, the prompt uses free stand-ins and names them, so the swap later is one change per family.
    5. The icon library, one of Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor or Remix.

    Four things in it that are not obvious

    • The approval gate is the point. A write into tier 1 cascades through 543 shipping tokens. Reviewing a ramp table costs a minute; reviewing a retoned file costs an afternoon, and by then the wrong neutral is already under everything.
    • A sibling, never a client area. Anything the client has and the kit lacks joins the category of its closest kit sibling, right after it, documented like the kit’s own. Step 8.6.
    • radius/md is not a pill. A client with pill buttons sets button/primary/radius to radius/full. Pushing radius/md to 999 turns every card, field and image into a capsule.
    • Leading cannot be bound. Figma reads a FLOAT bound to lineHeight as pixels, so the four type/leading rows stay documentation only. The prompt says so, to stop an agent trying.
    Brand adaptation prompt 
    You are adapting the Lazer DS Starter Kit to a client brand: its tokens, its
logo, everything in its old design system in step 8 and its photography in
step 9. I am a product designer and you have the
Figma MCP. Work in this file and nowhere else.

FIGMA FILE: [paste the file URL]

CLIENT SOURCES
  Old design system: [Figma link to the client’s existing design system, or
                      “none”. Read only. Its components, modules,
                      patterns and templates are audited in step 8.]
  Brandbook:         [Figma link, or brandbook pages placed on the Scratch page
                      of this file, or “none”. Read only.]
  Imagery:           [Figma link, a folder of images placed on the Scratch page
                      of this file, or “none”. Product shots, lifestyle and
                      editorial photography the client supplies. Read only.
                      Photos inside the old design system and the brandbook
                      count too, even when this line says none.]
  Fonts installed:   [“yes, on the machine running Figma” or “no, use free
                      stand-ins until they are”]
  Icon library:      [Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor or Remix]
  Overrides:         [optional: any value that must win over the sources]
You find everything else yourself in step 0: colours, typefaces and weights,
corner radius and the logo. Do not ask me to type a value that is already in
the sources. Ask only for what step 0 could not find.

WHAT YOU MAY EDIT
Through step 7: 01 Primitives, and nothing else. 120 of its 147 rows are load-bearing.
Change values in place. Never rename a row and never delete one: the row name
is the contract that tiers 2, 3 and 4 bind to.
You may add rows in one place only: color/<group>/<name>/<rung> for the extra
colour groups in step 1. <group> is the client’s own word for them (web,
category, pop, campaign), or palette if they have none. Add them with every
scope off, so they stay out of the property pickers, and the code name
var(--color-<group>-<name>-<rung>). Once I approve it in step 2, you may also
add a type/family or type/style row for a typeface the kit has no slot for.
On Foundations, Colour · Primitive ramps gains one ramp row per extra colour,
under a heading with the client’s group name, and the typed hex labels there
may be corrected. Token Reference is brought up to date in step 7. Nothing else
on those pages.
Until step 8, do not open 02 Semantic, 02 Spacing, 02 Motion, 03 Component
or 04 Responsive.
In 06 Icon Library you may only reorder modes, per step 5. Never edit its
variables or the icon drawings.
On the Components page you may edit the six Logo Slot variants, per step 5.
Anywhere in the file you may resize Logo Slot instances, per step 5B. Until
step 8, nothing else about a component changes: not its height, padding or
layout.
If the retone seems to need one of them, stop and tell me which role or rung is
missing instead of working around it.
Do not touch 05 Docs. It styles the documentation and never reaches a client
surface.
Leave space, stroke, duration and ease alone. Retone the brand, not the rhythm
and not the motion.
Step 8 widens this, and only once I approve its component map: you may then
edit and add the components, modules, patterns and templates the map names,
on the pages it names, and add or
repoint the 03 Component rows it lists. Never rename or delete a token, a
variant or a property, in step 8 or anywhere else.
Step 9 adds two more permissions: a Client imagery sheet on the Image System
page, and an image fill override on Image / Aspect Ratio instances. The main
Image / Aspect Ratio component itself never changes.

STEP 0: FIND EVERYTHING IN THE SOURCES BEFORE YOU DERIVE ANYTHING
Open every source read only and pull out:
  colour  every paint style, colour variable and colour frame or swatch page.
          In a brandbook placed as images, read the hex printed beside each
          swatch, and sample the swatch itself when the printed value disagrees.
  type    every text style, and every family and weight named in a type
          specimen, with tracking, case and line height where given.
  shape   corner radius on buttons, inputs, cards and images.
  logo    every lockup and mark, with its clear space rule, whether it
          exists as vectors or only as an image, and which grounds it has a
          version for: a dark logo for light grounds, a light logo for dark
          grounds and imagery, or both.
  system  every component, module, pattern, template and asset on every page
          of the client’s design system, by name, layer and page. Step 8
          audits them; here you only list them.
  imagery every raster photo in every source: the Imagery line, the old
          design system (inside instances too) and the brandbook. Count them
          per source page and say whether each reads as a product shot or a
          lifestyle or editorial photo. Step 9 migrates them; here you only
          count them.
Sort the colours into the client’s own groups: brand, accent, neutral, status,
and every other group, such as web or UI colours, category, pop, campaign,
social or illustration colours. Every group outside brand, accent, neutral and
status is an extra colour group. All of it is added under Foundations in
step 1 and step 3; none of it is left out because the kit has no slot for it.
Post one table, one line per item: what it is, where you found it (file, page
and frame), its value, and its destination in the kit: a rung, an extra ramp,
a type row, a radius row, the Logo Slot, the step 8 system map, the step 9
imagery library, or not carried, with the reason.
Nothing may drop out silently.
Below it, post NEEDS MANUAL ADD: every input you could not find in any source,
or found but cannot write through the connector. For each, say what is
missing, where it goes in the kit and how to add it by hand. For example: no
mono typeface in either source, keep IBM Plex Mono or name one; the logo exists
only as an image, paste vectors on the Scratch page; the logo has no version
for dark grounds, so you will make one in step 5 for the client to approve; the text family cannot be
loaded by the connector, follow the type hand-off in step 3; no status colours,
keep the kit defaults. If the sources disagree with each other or with
Overrides, list both values and ask which wins.

STEP 1: BUILD THE RAMPS BEFORE YOU WRITE ANYTHING
Step 0 gives you a handful of hexes. The system consumes specific rungs, so
derive complete ramps first:
  color/neutral   13 rungs: 0, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800,
                  900, 950, 1000. Every one is load-bearing. 800 is consumed
                  seven times and 0 and 900 six times each, so an error in
                  those three shows up everywhere.
  color/brand     7 rungs: 100, 200, 300, 500, 600, 700, 800. Client hex is 500.
  color/accent    4 rungs: 200, 300, 700, 800. The smallest surface in the kit.
  error           5 rungs: 100, 200, 500, 700, 800. The 200 is the only Dark
                  hover ground for a destructive action, so it cannot be skipped.
  success         4 rungs: 100, 500, 700, 800.
  warning         4 rungs: 100, 500, 700, 800.
  info            4 rungs: 100, 500, 700, 800.
  alpha/black     5 steps: 6, 10, 16, 40, 56. These are the elevation shadows.
                  Keep them unless the brand is unusually warm.
  color/chart     never hand picked. See step 5.
  extra colours   11 rungs each: 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800,
                  900, 950. One ramp for every colour in every extra group,
                  web colours included. The client hex sits at the rung nearest
                  its own lightness, not at 500, so a pale colour lands at 200
                  or 300. Nothing consumes these yet; they give a later surface,
                  badge or category tile tints to use.
  spare rungs     brand 50, 400, 900 and accent 50, 100, 400, 500, 600, 900
                  are not consumed, but the ramp sheet shows them. Fill them
                  from the same derivation so each sheet row reads as one ramp.
Step the ramps in a perceptual space (OKLCH) so the rungs are evenly spaced by
eye, and keep the client hex exactly as supplied at its own rung rather than
snapping it to a computed value.

STEP 2: STOP AND SHOW ME THE RAMPS
Post the step 0 table, NEEDS MANUAL ADD and the full ramp table, one hex per
rung and every extra colour included, before writing a single value. Flag
every rung you were unsure about. Then wait for my approval. Do not start
writing.

STEP 3: WRITE THE VALUES
On approval, write the approved hexes into 01 Primitives. It has one mode, Brand.
Values only.
Type is reached differently and this is the part that gets missed. type/family
(display, text, mono) and type/style (regular, medium, semibold, bold) are
consumed by TEXT STYLES, not by variable aliases. They look unused in an alias
graph and are the opposite of unused. Update those seven rows, then confirm the
eleven text styles resolve to the client typeface. Miss this and the client
ships with Inter.
Check the fonts first. Call figma.listAvailableFontsAsync and confirm every
family and style the styles would resolve to is listed. The connector cannot
write a family it cannot load. If one is missing, do not write the type rows
and do not swap in a look-alike on your own. Give me this hand-off instead,
filled in with the exact values:
  1. Install the licensed fonts on the machine running Figma desktop and
     restart Figma, so the font menu lists them.
  2. Local variables, 01 Primitives: set type/family/display and
     type/family/text to the family names exactly as the font menu spells them.
  3. Set type/style/regular, medium, semibold and bold to style names the
     families really have. If the display and text families name weights
     differently (Regular against 55 Roman), say which rows conflict: one
     shared row cannot serve both, and that is a decision for me.
  4. Tell me when it is done. You then re-read the eleven text styles and
     report the family and style each resolves to, and any missing font.
If I chose stand-ins, use the closest free family the connector lists, label
it a stand-in in DELIVER, and still give me the hand-off for the real fonts.
If the sources use a typeface the kit has no row for, such as a label or
caption face or a second display face, list it in NEEDS MANUAL ADD with the
row it would need (for example type/family/label) and which text styles would
use it. Adding it is my decision; once approved, add the row here and put it
on Token Reference in step 7.
Do not try to bind type/leading to lineHeight. Figma reads a FLOAT bound to
lineHeight as PIXELS, so 1.4 renders as 1.4px, and forcing the unit back to
percent silently drops the binding. Set line height as a literal value from the
kit’s lookup table and leave the four leading rows as the documented gap they are.
Radius: only sm, md, lg and full are consumed, and full stays at its pill value.
Never set md to a pill value. md is the default corner for cards, bars,
dialogs, tiles, tables and images across the kit, so a pill md turns all of
them into capsules. If the client’s buttons are pill, keep md at the client’s
container corner, 0 when it is square, and in step 8 point
button/primary/radius at radius/full.
Then add every extra colour group: create its rows as above, add one ramp row
per colour to Colour · Primitive ramps under a heading with the group name,
each chip bound to its variable and the client rung marked, and relabel the
typed hex labels on that sheet from the bound swatches. They are typed text
and go stale. Token Reference follows in step 7.

STEP 4: WALK IT IN DARK
Twenty rungs are Dark only, so a light mode review cannot catch them:
brand 200, brand 300, brand 800, accent 200, accent 300, neutral 400,
neutral 700, neutral 950, error 200, error 800, success 800, warning 800,
info 800, alpha/black 40, alpha/black 56, chart magenta 400, chart green 400,
chart violet 300, chart red 200, chart red 400.
Switch 02 Semantic to Dark and review every component sheet. All of them, not a
sample.

STEP 5: RE-DERIVE THE CHART PALETTE, SET THE ICON LIBRARY, PLACE THE LOGO
23 steps across 8 hues, computed rather than chosen. Run the palette validator
instead of judging separation by eye, fix every FAIL before moving on, re-derive
the series cap, and report the validator output to me.
Then set the icon library: in 06 Icon Library, drag the mode named in CLIENT
SOURCES to the first column so it becomes the file default. Do not change the
variables or any icon drawing.
Then place the logo. Open the Logo Slot set on the Components page. In
Size=Full and Size=Mark: delete the placeholder, clear the dashed stroke, and
put the vectors inside with every vector set to Scale constraints. Full keeps
its 40 height and takes the logo’s own width, so the artwork fills it edge to
edge with no margin of its own: resize Full to 40 times the logo’s aspect
ratio, without constraints, then place the vectors at 0, 0. Mark stays 40 by
40 with the mark centred. Spacing never lives inside the slot; it comes from
the component around it, in step 5B. If the logo is only an image, stop and
ask for vectors.
Logo Slot has three tones, and every one must read on its ground:
  Tone=Default    on page, nav and footer grounds. Fill logo/mark, which
                  follows text/default, so it is dark in Light mode and light
                  in Dark mode.
  Tone=Inverse    on surface/inverse, such as a dark utility bar or gift card.
                  Fill logo/mark-inverse, which flips the other way.
  Tone=On image   over a photo or scrim, such as the overlay header. Fill
                  logo/mark-on-image, which is light in both modes.
Put the client logo in all six variants, then make sure both versions exist,
from whatever the client supplied:
  One colour logo, dark only or light only: use the same vectors in every
    tone and bind them to that tone’s token. The tokens make the light and
    the dark version, so nothing is redrawn.
  Several colours, with a version for light grounds only: make the dark
    ground version for Inverse, On image and Dark mode. Use the client’s own
    reversed rule if the brandbook has one; otherwise knock the whole logo out
    to a single light colour bound to the tone’s token. Never invent new
    brand colours for it.
  Several colours, with a version for dark grounds only: do the reverse, a
    single dark colour for Default in Light mode.
  The client supplied both: place each where it belongs and bind nothing
    that would recolour it.
Any version you made rather than received goes in NEEDS MANUAL ADD as
needs client approval, with a screenshot of it on its ground.

STEP 5B: FIT THE LOGO TO EVERY COMPONENT THAT USES IT
A logo that fills its bar edge to edge looks cramped, and one that is too
small looks lost. Walk every Logo Slot instance inside a main component, not
inside another instance, and size it for its context. Always keep the aspect
ratio: width is height times the logo’s ratio.
  Bars: Site Header, Store Navbar, Nav, Mobile Menu, Nav Drawer, App Header. Logo height
  by bar height: 72 takes 32, 64 takes 28, 48 to 56 take 24, 44 takes 20.
  Measure the bar row that holds the logo, not the whole component, so a
  utility bar above it is not counted.
  Page Footer, Password Page, Gift Card Page: 40, which is the slot itself.
  Mark at 18 (Utility Bar, Buy Box) and 40 (Comparison): leave the size.
Set each instance’s tone from the ground under it, never by eye: resolve the
nearest filled ancestor’s token in Light and in Dark, and pick the first tone,
in the order Default, Inverse, On image, whose logo colour reaches 3:1 against
that ground in both modes. Swapping tone must keep the size you set. Some instances carry a stroke override
from the placeholder, so its dashed outline showed on dark grounds; clear any
stroke on a Logo Slot instance, or the client logo ships inside a box.
Then measure and report, per component and breakpoint:
  0. Ground contrast. The logo against the ground under it, Light and Dark,
     at least 3:1 in both, for every instance, overlay header included.
  1. Clear space. At least 12 above and below the logo inside its bar, and
     never less than the brandbook’s own clear space rule if it gives one.
  2. Prominence. The logo is the tallest item in the bar’s lead and never
     smaller than the table above. A wordmark with very heavy or very thin
     strokes may need 4 more or less; say which you changed and why.
  3. Width. A wide wordmark must not crowd the navigation. If it is wider
     than 240 on Desktop, 200 on Tablet or 160 on Mobile at its table height,
     step the height down by 4 until it fits, never below 20 on Desktop or 16
     on Mobile, and flag it: it probably needs a shorter lockup for small
     screens.
Placeholder Logo is only for third party logos: Logo Cloud, the Hero logo rows
and Comparison. Search every main component for a Placeholder Logo standing in
for the client’s own logo, such as the one in App Header, and swap it to Logo
Slot, sized by the table above.
Never change a bar’s height or padding to make a logo fit. If one cannot fit
by these rules, stop and tell me which component and breakpoint.

STEP 6: RE-MEASURE, WITH NUMBERS
Moving a ground changes what sits on it. Most of the checks below are invisible
to an automated token audit because neither side is text. Report a measured
ratio for each, not an impression:
  1. Text contrast. AA 4.5 for body, 7.0 on the primary and destructive
     grounds, 3.0 for anything non-text.
  2. Hairline perceptibility. A 1.2 floor for a decorative rule, against the
     ground behind it. Below that a 1px rule is invisible and nothing will warn
     you, because a rule is not text.
  3. Control boundaries. A 3.0 floor, not 1.2. border/strong is the resting
     boundary for every input, select, stepper, pagination button, swatch,
     checkbox, radio and secondary button, and border/strongest is the hover
     and selected state above it. field/background matches surface/page, so
     that border is the only thing saying where the input is. Lightening the
     neutral ramp can drop both below 3.0 without moving one text pair.
  4. Badge edges against the selected row. Every badge ground sits within three
     percent luminance of the selected row. A new brand hue changes which tones
     need their 1px edge.
  5. The three rule tokens: table/border, listrow/border and row-hover. These
     collided at ratio 1.00 once already.
  6. Destructive hover in Dark. It needs a rung between the error ramp’s 100
     and 500.
  7. The chart palette, per step 5.
  8. Dark on every component sheet.
  9. Icons in the chosen library, as rendered. Colour ratios do not change
     between libraries but the line does. Phosphor regular is the light one: a
     pair needs roughly 4.5 as a colour to stay above 3.0 at 16. Use the
     rendered check described on Iconography, Contrast by library.
  10. Logo tone, ground contrast in Light and Dark, clear space and size, per
      step 5B, one line per component and breakpoint.

STEP 7: UPDATE THE TOKEN REFERENCE
Token Reference lists every token with its value typed as text. It does not
follow the variables, so after a retone it still shows the kit, not the
client, and a new colour group or typeface is simply missing. Bring every
sheet on that page in line with the file:
  1. Tokens · 01 Primitives: relabel every hex from its bound swatch, and
     every type/family and type/style value from its variable, so Inter
     becomes the client family and each weight shows the client’s own style
     name.
  2. Every new colour group, such as web or category colours, gets a group
     card in the same format as the others: a header with the group path and
     its count, then one row per rung with the swatch bound to the variable,
     the rung and the hex. Put it in the shortest column and keep the groups
     in alphabetical order.
  3. Every new typeface row, such as type/family/label or a per-family weight
     row, gets a row in the type group with swatch, name and value like the
     others.
  4. Recount from the collections, not by hand: the header line of each sheet
     (tokens, groups, modes) and every group header count.
  5. Tokens · 02 Semantic, 03 Component and 04 Responsive: relabel every typed
     value from the variable as it now resolves, Light and Dark both where a
     sheet shows both.
  6. Tokens · 06 Icon Library: values are listed in mode order, so reorder
     them to match the mode order step 5 left.
Then check each sheet against its collection: every variable has exactly one
row, no row names a variable that does not exist, and no typed value differs
from the variable. Report the three counts per sheet. All three must be zero
misses. Anything you add uses Docs text styles.

STEP 8: AUDIT EVERYTHING IN THE CLIENT’S DESIGN SYSTEM AND BRING IT INTO THE KIT
Run this only when CLIENT SOURCES names an old design system. A brandbook alone
has nothing to audit here; say so and skip to step 9.
Tokens make the kit look like the client. They do not make it behave like the
client: a retoned navbar still carries the kit’s links, icons, case and height,
and a retoned homepage still has the kit’s sections in the kit’s order. This
step closes that gap for every layer of the client’s system, not only its
components.
THE RULE. When the client supplies its own design system, everything in it
ends up in the kit, every component, module, pattern, template and page:
  The same      the kit already has it. Keep the kit item, confirm the
                retone covers it, and update its copy and defaults to the
                client’s.
  Similar       the kit has an item that does the same job. Update and
                migrate the client’s version into that kit item, as a
                variant, property, layout or content. Never build a second
                item beside it.
  Missing       nothing in the kit does the job. Add it, built from kit
                components and tokens.
Nothing is skipped because it is large, slow or blocked by fonts. The only
exits are Not carried, with a reason I approve, and NEEDS MANUAL ADD, with
the exact blocker. This step is not finished until the coverage count in
8.9 shows every item accounted for.
  1. Inventory. Open every page of the old design system read only and list
     everything that reaches a client surface, in five layers:
       Components    buttons, inputs, cards, badges, tiles, nav items and
                     every other component set or standalone component.
       Modules       sections and blocks built from components: headers,
                     footers, heroes, product grids, carousels, banners,
                     editorial blocks, menus, modals, drawers.
       Patterns      flows and behaviours across screens: add to bag, search,
                     filtering, checkout, account, sign in, empty, error and
                     loading states, form validation, motion specs.
       Templates     whole pages and screens: homepage, listing, product
                     detail, bag, checkout, account, editorial, search, 404,
                     utility pages, transactional emails.
       Assets        custom icons, illustrations, image treatments and any
                     other library item the four layers above use.
                     Photography is counted here and migrated in step 9.
     For each item: name, layer, file, page and node, its variant properties
     and values, its breakpoints and its states. For a template, also list its
     sections in order and the component or module each one uses. Skip
     documentation furniture such as page headers, swatch cards and
     specimens, and say what you skipped.
  2. Map. Find the kit equivalent of each item by role, not by name: what it
     does and where it sits. Search every kit page that holds that layer:
       Components    Components, Iconography, Image System
       Modules       Global Modules, Landing Page Modules, Ecommerce Modules,
                     Dashboard Modules
       Patterns      Patterns, Interactions
       Templates     Templates, Shopify
     Grade each one:
       Match         same role and structure. The retone already covers it.
       Partial       same role, but the client’s version differs in
                     structure, content, copy, variants, states, size, or, for
                     a template, in its sections or their order.
       None          the kit has nothing that does this job.
       Not carried   a one off, a duplicate of another client item or a
                     campaign piece. Give the reason.
     For every Partial, list each difference on its own line, measured in
     both files. For example: lowercase labels against Title Case, text
     actions against icon and label, 52 high against 72, a transparent over
     image variant the kit lacks, a homepage that opens on a full bleed
     editorial hero where the kit opens on a split hero.
  3. Stop and post the CLIENT SYSTEM MAP, grouped by layer: one line per item
     with its source location, kit equivalent, grade, differences and the
     action you propose. Under it, list every token the changes would need
     that does not exist yet. Wait for my approval, line by line. Do not
     build anything.
  4. Work bottom up, because each layer is built from the one below it:
     components, then modules, then patterns, then templates. A module may
     only use kit components, a template only kit modules and components, so
     a client template that needs a missing module waits for that module.
     Similar is never left alone. Every Partial is migrated into the kit item
     it resembles: extend that kit component, module, pattern or template
     with the client’s variant, property, layout or content, such as a
     Tone=Dark, a Type=Collection or an italic accent in a headline, rather
     than building a second item beside it. A client item is similar when it
     does the same job with the same parts, however different it looks.
     Build a new item only when nothing in the kit does the job, and name the
     kit items you checked first. No Partial or None ends this step flagged,
     deferred or only listed: each is migrated or built, or named in NEEDS
     MANUAL ADD with its exact blocker. When the work is too large for one
     pass, split it into batches by layer, post each batch for my review,
     and keep a done column on the map so nothing drops between batches.
     Text edits need fonts the connector can load. If the client fonts are
     not loadable, point the type/family and type/style rows at free
     stand-ins while you build, and at the end hand me the exact values to
     set back in desktop.
  5. Update each approved Partial in place:
       Add what the client has: a variant, a property, a state, a layout.
       Change default copy, case, labels and slot content to the client’s.
       Change size or padding only to a value the client file specifies, and
       only through an existing space, size or radius token.
       For a module, swap in the right component variants and set its slot
       content; for a pattern, update its states and the spec beside it; for
       a template, reorder, add or remove its section instances to match the
       client’s page.
       Update its documentation in the same pass: the variant count and
       property list on its Variants label, its Spec rows, its Dark mode
       panel when a new variant appears, and one Notes line that starts
       Client migration and names the source page and node.
       Never delete or rename a variant, property or layer that an instance
       elsewhere in the file uses. Instances across the module pages and
       templates depend on them, and a rename silently drops every override.
       Swapping an instance to another variant keeps its text only when the
       text layers in both share a name. Check every label after a swap; if
       one went back to its default, swap back, which restores it, and match
       the layer names first.
       Text weight, size, case and style edits need the client fonts loaded
       in the connector, and so does cloning any variant that contains text.
       If they are not loaded, do every other change and list each blocked
       one in NEEDS MANUAL ADD: item, variant, layer and target style.
  6. Build each approved None in the kit’s conventions:
       It goes on the page where its kit siblings live, inside the category
       its closest kit sibling belongs to and right after that sibling: a
       component after its neighbour in the same Group, a module in the same
       Section as the module it extends, a template right after the kit
       template it varies. Its label names that category, such as MODULE ·
       PRODUCT or TEMPLATE · PRODUCT PAGE · CLIENT VARIANT. Never append
       client items at the end of a page or in a separate client area. Add
       it to that page’s index and its Components used list, and update the
       page’s counts.
       Auto layout throughout. Every fill, stroke, radius, gap and padding is
       bound to an existing 02 Semantic or 03 Component token, every text
       uses a kit text style, every icon is an Icon instance from 06 Icon
       Library, every logo is a Logo Slot instance and every image uses the
       kit’s image component. No raw hex and no raw font.
       Modules and templates are built from instances, never from detached
       copies.
       Breakpoint variants (Desktop, Tablet, Mobile) when the client version
       changes across them, using the kit’s property names: Breakpoint,
       State, Size, Tone. Templates get a frame per breakpoint, like the
       kit’s own.
       A pattern gets its states laid out side by side with a short spec in
       Docs text styles, like the kit’s Patterns and Interactions sheets.
       A custom client icon the kit’s libraries lack goes in NEEDS MANUAL
       ADD with where it is used; do not draw icons into 06 Icon Library.
       A component description in the kit’s format.
       Documented exactly like its kit siblings, never on a grab bag sheet of
       client additions. Each component and module gets its own section,
       Component · <name> or Module · <name>, on docs/surface/page with
       Docs text styles and docs tokens only:
         Header      a Docs/Label category line, the name in Heading/H4
                     and a Docs/Body description.
         Variants    the set on a docs/surface/inset panel, labelled with
                     its variant count and properties.
         Breakpoints for a module, a frame per breakpoint pinned to its
                     04 Responsive mode, like Paired frames.
         Dark mode   the variants again in a frame set to Dark.
         Rule, then Spec: variants and values, the tier 3 tokens it uses,
                     and for a module what it composes and borrows.
         Notes       a docs/surface/card panel; the first line says Client
                     addition and names the source page and node.
       A template gets the kit template sheet: Header, a DESKTOP · 1440
       frame, Tablet and mobile, Rule, Spec (bands in order, breakpoints,
       the instances it composes), Shopify (theme file, how it lands, scope
       note) and Notes, never a single source line.
       A pattern gets a Header, its states side by side, a Spec (trigger,
       components it uses, the end state) and Notes, on the Patterns or
       Interactions page beside the kit’s own.
       Add every new section to its page index and to the Components used
       list of each template that uses it.
  7. Tokens. A change that needs a role the kit lacks, such as an image
     radius apart from the button radius, or a category tile ground, goes in
     the map rather than being invented on the spot. Once I approve it, add
     the row to 03 Component, or point an existing 03 Component row at a
     different primitive, and put it on Token Reference per step 7. Never
     change what an existing 02 Semantic role means.
  8. Check every item you touched or added:
       Every instance of it in the file still renders: none collapsed to its
       content, none clipped, no override lost. Compare instance count and
       sizes before and after.
       Light and Dark, with the step 6 measures run on it.
       A raw paint scan: zero unbound fills or strokes, apart from content
       such as product swatches and flags, which you name.
       Every breakpoint at its frame width, with nothing overflowing.
       Each template side by side with the client’s page it maps to.
       Every item you added or migrated has its full documentation section,
       and no grab bag sheet of client additions is left anywhere.
  9. Coverage. Recount the client file and report, per layer and page:
     items found, the same, migrated, added, not carried and blocked. Every
     found item must sit in exactly one of those columns, and the done
     column on the map must match. Name every item still open. If any are,
     the step is not done: continue with the next batch rather than closing
     the run.

STEP 9: MIGRATE THE CLIENT’S IMAGERY
Run this whenever any source holds client photography: the Imagery line, the
old design system or the brandbook. Retoned templates full of grey ratio
placeholders still do not look like the client; their own photos do. If no
source holds a single photo, say so, leave the kit placeholders in place and
skip to HOW TO WORK. Never fill a slot with stock, generated or other
third party images unless I ask for it.
  1. Collect. List every raster image in every source, with its image hash,
     source page and node, size, and how the client used it: a product shot
     (product cards, grids, swipers, bag lines, swatches, thumbnails) or a
     lifestyle or editorial photo (heroes, banners, feature rows, articles).
     Leave out full page screenshots, UI screenshots and icons under 90px,
     and say what you left out.
  2. Transfer the original files, never a screenshot or an export of the
     frame they sit in. The connector cannot copy an image fill from one
     file to another, so:
       download_assets on client nodes of 20 images or fewer returns each
       raw image URL. It cannot target a layer inside an instance; use the
       nearest node that is not one.
       Fetch the bytes where figma.com is reachable, from the shell or, when
       its network blocks figma.com, from a browser tab on figma.com. Ask me
       before you use a browser.
       Hash the bytes with SHA-1: that is Figma’s image hash, so you can match
       every file to the catalogue and drop duplicates.
       upload_assets with target node ids places each one on its library
       tile in this file. Recount after every batch.
     An image you cannot reach goes in NEEDS MANUAL ADD with its hash, its
     source page and node, and the exact blocker.
  3. Library. On the Image System page, beside the kit sheets, build one
     sheet named Client imagery · <client>, in the format of the other sheets
     on that page, with Docs text styles and docs tokens only:
       A header (label, title, a short intro), a stats row (photos
       migrated, product shots, lifestyle photos, slots filled), how to use
       cards (product slots, hero and editorial slots, swapping an image),
       and a not migrated card naming every open item.
       Then one card per client source page: its name, its photo count, the
       templates and module pages that use it, and two rows, Product shots
       and Lifestyle. Each tile is the photo at its own proportion, image
       radius 0, captioned with the nearest kit ratio and its type, such as
       3:4 · Product. Name each tile <client>/<P or L>/<hash>.
  4. Apply. Every Image / Aspect Ratio instance in the templates, modules,
     patterns and components gets a client photo as an instance fill
     override, scale mode Fill, with Show labels and Show ratio off.
       Each template takes its photos from the client page it maps to in the
       step 8 map: the PDP from the client’s product pages, Editorial from
       their editorial pages, and so on, falling back to the whole library.
       Product slots take product shots; heroes and wide slots take
       lifestyle photos. Vary the picks so neighbours do not repeat.
       Photos only ever go in the kit’s image component. Never put an image
       fill on a frame, card or section, and never change the main Image /
       Aspect Ratio component: it keeps documenting the ratios.
  5. Check. Count Image / Aspect Ratio instances per page against those you
     filled: zero placeholders left in any template. Screenshot each template
     beside the client page it maps to. Confirm nothing resized, clipped or
     lost an override, and that Dark still reads over every photo with text.

HOW TO WORK
Load the figma-use skill before every use_figma call, every time, not just the
first.
Read the current value of a primitive before overwriting it, and tell me what
you are replacing.
If a screenshot and the node geometry disagree, trust the geometry. Inline
screenshots can render stale.
Documentation you add uses Docs text styles only. The kit’s own styles retype
to the client font, and once that font is missing the connector cannot edit
them.
Any copy you write into the file follows the house rules: no em dashes and no en
dashes, middle dots for label separators only, nothing below 13px in
documentation copy, and no straight double quotes or angle brackets in component
descriptions because Figma escapes both.

DELIVER
  1. The step 0 table, NEEDS MANUAL ADD and the ramp table from step 2,
     approved by me before any write.
  2. Exactly which rows changed, old value to new value, and every row added.
  3. The re-measure report from step 6, a ratio per line.
  4. A screenshot of Store Navbar, Site Header (the overlay layout included)
     and Page Footer with the logo in place, Light and Dark, the step 5B
     table, and every logo version you made rather than received.
  5. The typeface hand-off from step 3, if any font was missing, and which
     rows are stand-ins.
  6. The step 7 check per Token Reference sheet, with every group card and
     row you added.
  7. The step 8 client system map as I approved it, by layer; each component,
     module, pattern and template updated, with its changes; each one added,
     with its page and node and a link to its documentation section; every token row added or repointed; and the step
     8 check, with a screenshot of each in Light and Dark and each template
     beside the client page it maps to.
     The step 8.9 coverage table, with every open item named.
  8. The step 9 imagery report: photos found per source, migrated, left out
     and why, and not migrated with hash and blocker; slots filled per page
     out of the total; a link to the Client imagery sheet; and a screenshot
     of each template with its photos in place.
  9. Anything you could not do, named plainly rather than worked around.

    The same prompt on the Governance page in Figma

    Why it is shaped this way

    1. 01

      The approval gate in step 2 is the whole point. A write into 01 Primitives cascades through 543 shipping tokens. Reviewing a ramp table costs a minute. Reviewing a retoned file costs an afternoon, and by then the wrong neutral is already under everything.

    2. 02

      Ramps before values, because a client hands over three hexes and the system consumes about sixty rungs. A designer who opens Primitives first invents rungs one at a time, in whatever order the variable list happens to be sorted. Naming the rungs up front turns the derivation into a task with an end.

    3. 03

      Step 3 is there because type has a second consumption path. The seven type rows are reached by text styles rather than by aliases, so every tool that checks alias coverage reports them as unused. The failure mode is quiet: the client ships with Inter.

    4. 04

      Step 6 asks for numbers because looks fine is how the three rule tokens collided at ratio 1.00. Most of the re-measure list is invisible to an automated audit, because neither side of the comparison is text. A 1px rule that vanishes against its ground will not raise a single warning.

    5. 05

      Step 8 maps before it builds, because a retone fixes how the system looks and not what it is. The stress test retoned goop cleanly and the navbar still read as the kit: Title Case links, icons beside the actions, 72 high. Grading every client component, module, pattern and template against its kit equivalent first turns that into a list to approve, and the rule against renaming variants keeps every instance across the modules intact.

    6. 06

      Step 9 moves the photos, because grey placeholders still read as the kit. The goop stress test had the right tokens, components and templates, and every image slot was still a labelled grey ratio. The connector cannot copy an image fill between files, so the step spells out the transfer, keeps the original files rather than screenshots, and only ever fills the kit’s image component, so the main component keeps documenting the ratios.

    What it deliberately does not cover. Logo rules such as clear space, minimum size and lockup variants, imagery art direction, tone of voice, and anything else specific to one client. Those belong in the project file that inherits the kit, not in the kit’s own adaptation pass. Scope here is colour, type and radius, the supplied logo in the Logo Slot so every header and footer carries it, and the client’s own components, modules, patterns and templates where an old design system supplies them.

    Go deeper: Read Me, adaptation checklist, the full thirteen step sequence, and the adaptation runbook, every rung the system consumes, the twenty Dark only rungs and the re-measure list.

    Client additions go in a category

    Step 8.6. When a client brings a component, module, template or pattern the kit lacks, it joins the category of its closest kit sibling, right after it, documented exactly like the kit’s own. Never a separate Client additions sheet, and never a run of client items at the end of a page.

    LayerWhere it goesThe rule
    ComponentIts sibling’s Group, after itInside the Group of the closest kit component on the Components page, labelled with that category (COMPONENT · METADATA). Add a Component index row and update the page count. Category Label sits after Tag in Data display.
    ModuleIts sibling’s Section, after itInside the Section of the module it extends, right after it, labelled MODULE · PRODUCT, MODULE · CART and so on. Purchase Option after Buy Box; Shipping Progress after Cart Drawer.
    TemplateAfter the kit template it variesStraight after the kit template of the same page type: TEMPLATE · PRODUCT PAGE · CLIENT VARIANT. A page type the kit lacks joins the closest category as CLIENT ADDITION; Checkout and Account follow Cart.
    PatternBeside the kit pattern it extendsPatterns or Interactions page, with Header, states side by side, Spec and Notes.
    ImageryClient imagery sheetImage System page, grouped by the client’s source page. Photos only fill the kit image component.
    Every itemFull kit documentationHeader, Variants, breakpoint frames for a module, Dark mode, Rule, Spec and Notes, whose first line reads Client addition, with source page and node. Update the page overview and every Components used list.
    Why. A client area hides its items from anyone browsing by category, and it drifts away from the page indexes and counts within a week. Placed by category, a client addition is found where a designer already looks, and the next client inherits it as a candidate kit item.

    Where each kind of addition goes

    LayerWhere it goesThe rule
    ComponentIts sibling’s Group, after itOn the Components page, inside the Group of the closest kit component and right after it, never at the end of the page. Label it with that category, such as COMPONENT · METADATA, add a row to the Component index and update the page count. Category Label sits after Tag in Data display.
    ModuleIts sibling’s Section, after itOn the module page, inside the Section and Sheets of the module it extends, right after that module, with a label such as MODULE · PRODUCT or MODULE · CART. Purchase Option sits after Buy Box in Product; Shipping Progress after Cart Drawer in Cart and Checkout.
    TemplateAfter the kit template it variesOn the Templates row, straight after the kit template of the same page type. A variant reads TEMPLATE · PRODUCT PAGE · CLIENT VARIANT; a page type the kit lacks joins the closest category as CLIENT ADDITION, so Checkout and Account follow Cart.
    PatternBeside the kit pattern it extendsOn the Patterns or Interactions page, next to the kit pattern or interaction it builds on, with a Header, its states side by side, a Spec and Notes.
    ImageryClient imagery sheetOn the Image System page, one Client imagery sheet grouped by the client’s source page. Photos only ever fill the kit’s image component.
    Every itemFull kit documentationHeader, Variants, breakpoint frames for a module, Dark mode, Rule, Spec and Notes, with a first Notes line that says Client addition and names the source page and node. Update the page overview and every Components used list that includes it.
    Never a client area. A separate Client additions sheet, or a run of client items at the end of a page, hides them from anyone browsing by category and drifts from the page’s indexes and counts. In the goop stress test, thirteen client components and modules and twenty five templates started that way and were moved into their categories.

    Client imagery

    Step 9. The connector cannot copy an image fill between files, so each photo is downloaded from the source, hashed and uploaded into the copy, then placed on a Client imagery sheet on the Image System page, grouped by the client page it came from. Every Image / Aspect Ratio instance then takes a photo as an instance override. Never a fill on a frame, and the main component keeps documenting ratios. Photos that only exist inside nested instance overrides are listed in NEEDS MANUAL ADD rather than screenshotted.

    The rules on the Image system page

    Worked example: the goop stress test

    A separate file, not the kit. Everything below happened in a duplicate made for the test. Nothing from goop is in the Lazer DS Starter Kit, and nothing on the other pages of this site comes from it.

    The prompt was stress tested on a duplicate of the kit against goop’s old design system, a mature retail system with its own components, editorial modules and twenty five page templates. It is the reference run: what a full adaptation produces and where it went wrong.

    194client items audited
    192covered by the kit or built
    13client components and modules placed
    25client templates placed
    259photos migrated
    3,157image instances filled

    Two items needed a manual add, both custom icons outside every library the kit switches between. Six photos were left in NEEDS MANUAL ADD.

    What it taught the prompt

    Fonts the connector cannot load

    Figma refuses to write a type/family value for a font it cannot load, so goop’s licensed faces had to be set by hand on a machine with them installed. One shared type/style row cannot be both 55 Roman and Regular either, so two families with different style names need per family weight rows.

    radius/md is not the pill

    Pushing radius/md to a pill value for goop’s buttons turned cards, tables and images into capsules. The fix is a role split at the component tier: image/radius and table/radius on radius/none, and pill buttons through button/primary/radius on radius/full. Step 3 now says so.

    A placeholder logo survived

    The Dashboard template still showed the kit brand, because App Header used a Placeholder Logo rather than a Logo Slot. Step 5B now searches every main component for one standing in for the client’s logo.

    Raw Inter text

    286 text layers in main components had Inter typed by hand, with no style and no binding, so they never retoned. They were bound to type/family and type/style in the copy. The same defect is in the original kit.

    Category colours

    goop tags Fashion, Beauty, Wellness and Home by colour. They went in as a new Category group in 01 Primitives at goop’s exact values, with a ramp row and a Token Reference card. Using them as backgrounds will need semantic roles.

    A client area drifts

    Thirteen client components and modules and twenty five templates first landed on their own sheets. They were moved into their categories, which is where the placement rule came from.

    Copy for Claude

    Two blocks to paste into Claude with the Figma MCP connected. The runbook is the rules of the kit, for reviewing a retone, adding client items or answering what is allowed. The brand adaptation prompt is the full ten step procedure that runs an adaptation end to end.

    Adaptation runbook

    The governance rules as a prompt: what to edit, the rungs a palette must supply, the Dark only rungs, the re-measure list, the traps, the icon library and the client additions rule. Fill the two lines at the top.
