     Read it

    Adaptation runbook 
    You are helping me adapt or review a copy of the Lazer DS Starter Kit in Figma.
Treat this runbook as the rules of the kit. I am a product designer and you
have the Figma MCP. Work only in the file I give you, and never in the master
kit (JImp972lwOgzmFtQyC2PO2): adaptations always run in a duplicate.

FIGMA FILE: [paste the URL of the client copy]
TASK: [retone to a client brand / review a retone / add client items / other]

THE SHORT VERSION
Edit 01 Primitives and nothing else. 120 of its 147 rows are load bearing: 112 reached through variable aliases and 8 through text styles. Change values
in place. Never rename and never delete a token, because a token name is the
contract every tier above depends on. The kit carries one brand mode, Brand.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS
1. Build the ramps before touching a token. A client gives three hexes; the
   system consumes specific rungs, so first turn the hexes into full ramps
   that hit every rung listed below.
2. Check the ramps can carry the contrast obligations before binding anything.
3. Retone 01 Primitives only, in place.
4. Re-derive the chart palette rather than picking it: 23 steps across 8 hues.
   Run the validator per mode, snap each slot to the nearest passing step,
   then work out the series cap again.
5. Walk the re-measure list below, with numbers.
6. Look at every Dark block. Twenty rungs are consumed only in Dark.

WHAT THE CLIENT PALETTE HAS TO SUPPLY
color/neutral: 0 50 100 200 300 400 500 600 700 800 900 950 1000, all 13.
  800 is consumed seven times, 0 and 900 six times each.
color/brand: 100 200 300 500 600 700 800 (50, 400 and 900 spare).
color/accent: 200 300 700 800.
color/utility/error: 100 200 500 700 800. The 200 is the only Dark hover
  ground for a destructive action.
color/utility/success, warning, info: 100 500 700 800 each.
color/alpha/black: 6 10 16 40 56, the elevation shadows.
color/chart: 23 steps across 8 hues, computed, never hand picked.
type/family (display, text, mono) and type/style (regular, medium, semibold,
  bold): consumed by text styles, not aliases, so an alias audit shows them as
  unused. Miss them and the client ships in Inter.
radius: sm md lg full. radius/md is the default corner for cards, bars,
  dialogs, tiles, tables and images. Never set md to a pill value. If the
  client's buttons are pills, point button/primary/radius at radius/full.
space, duration, ease: leave alone. Retone colour, not rhythm or motion.

THE DARK ONLY RUNGS
color/brand/200, 300, 800; color/accent/200, 300; color/neutral/400, 700, 950;
color/utility/error/200, 800; color/utility/success/800; warning/800; info/800;
color/alpha/black/40, 56; color/chart/magenta/400, green/400, violet/300,
red/200, red/400. Nothing in Light points at them, so a Light review cannot
catch them.

THE RE-MEASURE LIST
1. Text contrast: 4.5 for body, 7.0 on the primary and destructive grounds,
   3.0 for anything non text.
2. Hairlines: 1.2 floor for a decorative rule against its ground.
3. Control boundaries at 3.0: border/strong and border/strongest against
   field/background and surface/page, in both modes. field/background matches
   surface/page, so the border is the only thing marking an input.
4. Badge edges against the selected row: badge/info/background against
   brand/100 measured 1.005 once.
5. table/border, listrow/border and row-hover collided at 1.00 once.
6. Destructive hover in Dark needs a rung between error 100 and 500.
7. The chart palette, re-derived.
8. Dark mode on every component sheet.

WHAT YOU NEVER EDIT
Tiers 2, 3 and 4. If a retone has you opening 02 Semantic you are either
adding a role the system lacks, which is rare and fine, or working around a
ramp missing a rung, which is the real problem. 05 Docs styles the
documentation and never reaches a client surface.

KNOWN TRAPS
- type/leading cannot be bound. Figma reads a FLOAT bound to lineHeight as
  pixels, so the four leading rows stay documentation only. Do not try.
- Fonts the connector cannot load cannot be written into type/family. Use a
  free stand in, name it, and hand me the exact values for the real face.
- Text typed in Inter with no style and no binding never retones. Search main
  components for it and bind fontFamily and fontStyle to the type variables.
- Placeholder Logo is only for third party logos (Logo Cloud, Hero logo rows,
  Comparison). Swap any that stand in for the client's own logo to Logo Slot.

ICON LIBRARY
The icon set switches between Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor and Remix through the
06 Icon Library collection. Set the mode on a page or frame, or make it the
file default by dragging it to the first column in the Variables panel. Names
stay Lucide in every mode. A client file ships one library, never a mixture.
Phosphor regular draws lighter: a pair needs roughly 4.5 as a colour to stay
above 3.0 once drawn at 16.

CLIENT ADDITIONS GO IN A CATEGORY
Anything the client has that the kit lacks joins the category of its closest
kit sibling, right after it, documented exactly like the kit's own. Never a
separate client additions sheet and never a run of client items at the end
of a page.
- Component: inside its sibling's Group on the Components page, labelled with
  that category (COMPONENT · METADATA), plus a Component index row and an
  updated page count.
- Module: inside the Section of the module it extends, right after it,
  labelled MODULE · PRODUCT, MODULE · CART and so on.
- Template: straight after the kit template of the same page type, labelled
  TEMPLATE · PRODUCT PAGE · CLIENT VARIANT. A page type the kit lacks joins
  the closest category as CLIENT ADDITION.
- Pattern: beside the kit pattern it extends, with Header, states, Spec and
  Notes.
- Imagery: a Client imagery sheet on the Image System page, grouped by the
  client's source page. Photos only fill Image / Aspect Ratio instances as
  overrides; never a fill on a frame, and the main component never changes.
- Every item: Header, Variants, breakpoint frames for a module, Dark mode,
  Rule, Spec and Notes, whose first line reads Client addition with the
  source page and node. Update the page overview and every Components used
  list.

HOUSE RULES FOR ANYTHING YOU WRITE INTO THE FILE
No em dashes and no en dashes; a middle dot separates label parts. Nothing
below 13px in documentation copy. No straight double quotes or angle brackets
in component descriptions. Documentation text uses the Docs text styles.

HOW TO REPORT
Before writing, show me what you plan to change and wait for my yes. After
writing, report each re-measure line with a measured ratio in both modes,
list anything you could not do, and name it plainly rather than working
around it.

    Adaptation runbook sheet in Figma

    Claude skills

    Six skills turn the kit’s own procedures into something Claude runs for you, all in Figma. The audit, adaptation and new module skills are how the kit is maintained; create, inspire and refine are optional helpers. Each one reads the Figma file for its rules, so they stay in step with the kit. They need the Figma connector in Claude, and they work on the kit or any client copy of it.

    Download a zip and upload it in the skills section of Claude’s settings, one skill per zip. Each designer adds them to their own account. After that they work in any Claude chat, and you don’t have to remember their names: just ask in plain words.

    Kit audit

    lazer-kit-audit

    Ask “audit the starter kit”. Checks tokens, bindings, the width test across every breakpoint range, templates, doc counts and the copy rules. Reports first, fixes only what you approve, then brings the doc pages and this site back in line.

    Download zip

    Adaptation and rollout

    Two things live here. The adaptation runbook is the colour depth behind the Read Me checklist: which rungs a client palette has to supply, and what has to be re-measured once it does. The rollout tracker is generalised from a past client's status tracker, which worked well enough to keep verbatim in shape. Seed it at step 11 of the adaptation checklist so sequencing and sign-off come with the kit rather than being reinvented per project.

    The rollout tracker

    Eight columns, each earning its place. Design and dev status are tracked separately because they diverge, and one merged column hides where the work actually is.

    ColumnWhy it exists
    TouchpointOrganised by where a thing lives on the site rather than by component type. A stakeholder can find their own page; nobody goes looking for "Badge".
    PriorityP1 / P2 / P3. Kept separate from readiness: an urgent thing can be unfinished and a finished thing can be low priority.
    Design statusNot started / In progress / Complete. Tracked independently of dev, because they diverge.
    Dev statusThe same scale, owned by engineering. Keeping it separate from design status is the whole point, because one merged column hides where the work actually is.
    WaveWave 1 / Wave 2 / On Hold / Removed. Phases the build so nobody starts a template before its chrome exists.
    Approved?A lightweight sign-off gate before anything moves to dev. One column, one owner, no ceremony.
    NotesPlain language: what is left to do, written as a sentence someone can act on. A status word does not tell anyone anything.
    Figma nodeThe node ID. It costs ten seconds to fill in and saves a dev hunting for the frame.

    Wave model

    Wave 1

    Global chrome

    Nav, utility bar, footer. Every template depends on this, so it migrates first, always, on every project.

    Wave 2

    Templates

    Listing pages, detail pages, content and storytelling. Each needs Wave 1 in place and its own stakeholder sign-off.

    On hold

    Blocked

    Waiting on a decision, an asset, or a stakeholder. Naming it as held keeps it from sitting unfinished with no explanation.

    Removed

    Explicitly out of scope. Writing down what was cut is what keeps it from being re-litigated in week six.

    The invariant

    Tier 1 primitives are the entire adaptation surface. Any change that puts a raw value above tier 1, or a hex on a layer, breaks the kit. That is the one rule with no exceptions, and it is the reason a retone is a day of work rather than a month.

    House rules

    These are enforced, and they exist because each one was a real problem first.

    • Nothing below 13px in documentation copy. Product type inside a component keeps its real size.
    • The kit's own ramps stay neutral. Any client derived colour lives in 05 Docs and styles documentation chrome only.
    • surface/selected is the one documented exception: a brand tint, because no neutral reads as chosen.
    • Component descriptions carry no straight double quotes and no angle brackets. Figma escapes both.
    • A panel with a 1px inside stroke turns on strokesIncludedInLayout, so full-bleed children are inset by the border instead of painting over it. Clip the panel too, or a square-cornered row escapes the radius.
    • Image plates carry an aspect ratio lock. Image / Aspect Ratio is a fixed plate, not a ratio, so a plate that fills its width while holding a fixed height stops holding its ratio the moment a module is resized. Lock it and the height follows the width.

    Adding to the kit

    A new token either role

    1. Name the decision, not the value. If you cannot say what the row is for without naming a colour, it belongs a tier lower.
    2. Put it in the right tier. A role goes in 02 Semantic. A component decision goes in 03 Component and aliases a role. A new value goes in 01 Primitives.
    3. Give it every mode. A semantic row without a dark value is a bug that ships silently.
    4. Re-measure what sits on it. When a ground moves, the rules and labels on it have to be checked again. A luminance identical pair is invisible and no contrast audit flags it, because neither one is text.

    A new component either role

    1. Check it is not a variant. Most new components are an axis on a set that already exists.
    2. Build it from sets you have. Compose Icon, Badge, Avatar and Control rather than redrawing them.
    3. Write the description. What it is for, and where it stops. A set with no description is not finished.
    4. Give it a dark block and an interaction entry. If its behaviour cannot answer the six questions, the component is not specified yet.

    What ships and what does not

    LayerShipsWhy
    01 to 04 and 06Yes, 538 rowsThe system a client project consumes.
    05 DocsNo, 27 rowsDocumentation chrome only. It is the one place a client derived colour is allowed, and it never reaches a product surface.
    Component setsYes, 69Published as one library, with the 7 Iconography sets.
    Module setsYes, 87Global is required. Landing, Ecommerce and Dashboard are optional and delete in one action.
    TemplatesYes, 9Built from module instances only, at three breakpoints.
    Effect stylesYes, 4Elevation binds its colour to a token, so it retones with everything else.
    Scratch pageNoWorking surface. Empty it before publishing.

    Open questions

    • Secondary button hover in dark mode. button/secondary/background-hover recedes in dark, from #242628 to #131415, while every other interactive ground comes forward. Left as it is pending a decision, because it may be the right answer for a ground that is already dark.
    • The Playbook palette. The colours derived from a past client in 05 Docs need a call on reuse before anything leaves the studio.
    • Iconography in dark mode. The Icon set is 146 variants on its own page, so it carries no dark block. Every component that uses an icon does.
    • Promoting client additions. A client addition that recurs across engagements is a candidate kit item. Nobody owns that call yet.
    • Publishing. The file is still in team drafts. It moves out and publishes as a library before a project consumes it.

    Delivery status

    Status

    Where every component and module stands, so designers, developers and the client see the same picture: what is still moving, what is waiting for sign off, and what can be built. Set in Figma on each sheet; this page mirrors it.

    156 items · 69 components and 87 modules · synced from Figma Sep 29, 2026

    Every item

    NameTypeWhereStatusFigma

    What each status means

    WIP

    The designer is still working on it. Do not build from it yet.

    In review

    Design is done and waiting for sign off. Only small changes expected.

    Ready for dev

    Approved, with every variant, state, breakpoint and token in place. Build from it.

    Final

    Built in code and checked against the design at every breakpoint and in Dark.

    Designers set WIP and In review. The lead designer moves an item to Ready for dev after sign off, and whoever checks the build sets Final. Anything new, including a client addition, starts at WIP. To change a status, select the Status tag under the item’s title in Figma and switch its Status property; the Status tracking sheet on the Governance page explains the same rules.
